### A536 · P3 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-20 (CI only) · The end-to-end suites run every night against DEV, and never against production
Closes A189 (the suites existed and ran nowhere). **BUILT:** `.github/workflows/nightly-e2e.yml` — 23:30 UTC (02:30
Nairobi) and on demand (choose the API suites, Playwright on/off); a separate workflow, ci.yml untouched, so it never
blocks a push or a pull request; the run goes red when a suite fails. Steps: the production guard + a wait of up to 3 min
for the dev API's `/health` (Render sleeps) → `tests/runner.mjs` (auth, data, orders, reports, security, permissions,
restaurant) → `e2e/seed/seed-staff-api.mjs` (new: the Waiter role and the manager / supervisor / cashier / waiter test
staff through the owner API only — no browser, no database, idempotent; logins to `$GITHUB_ENV`) → `npx playwright test`
(Chromium) with the HTML report and failure traces as an artifact (14 days); the run's summary lists each part.
**The guard** — `e2e/lib/prod-guard.mjs`, called by every entry point (the runner, both Playwright configs, the staff
seed, the workflow's first step); no override; exit 3: refuses `zaptill.co.ke` and every host under it (production and
every client's address) unless the label next to the domain is `dev`/`staging` (`dev.zaptill.co.ke`, `dev-api.…`,
`app.dev.…`), the production Render (`swiftpos-server`, `swiftpos-prod-mype`) and Vercel (`swiftpos-dashboard`,
`swiftpos-admin`, `swiftpos-admin-eta`) hosts, `E2E_EXTRA_PROD_HOSTS`, an address that does not parse; then refuses a
`/health` without `env` or with `env: production` (production hides env); and the test browser starts with
`--host-resolver-rules` that make every production host unresolvable, so a dashboard built with a production API cannot
sell into a live business. **Configurable:** variables `E2E_API_URL` (default the dev API `swiftpos-20c2.onrender.com`),
`E2E_WEB_URL` (the dev dashboard — Playwright is skipped with a warning until it is set), `E2E_ADMIN_URL` (guarded, no
admin specs yet), `E2E_EXTRA_PROD_HOSTS`; secrets `E2E_OWNER_EMAIL`, `E2E_OWNER_PASSWORD` (the owner of a dedicated test
business on DEV). The runner also reads `E2E_API_URL` / `E2E_OWNER_EMAIL` / `E2E_OWNER_PASSWORD`, the Playwright configs
`E2E_WEB_URL` / `E2E_API_URL`. Not posted to the admin System page: ops events accept only `deploy_check` / `vuln_scan`.
**Owner, once:** a dedicated restaurant test business on DEV (web access on, sign-in codes off), the dev dashboard built
against the dev API, the two secrets and `E2E_WEB_URL` — `docs/E2E-NIGHTLY.md`. Tests:
`tests/e2e-prod-guard-a536.test.mjs` (35; production refused / dev passes, /health, the command line's exit 3, the wiring;
mutation-checked). The guard was run by hand: the production API, dashboard and admin refused (exit 3) by the guard, the
runner and the seed; the dev API passed and answered `env: development`.

### A533 · P2 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-20 (till 1.0.20 + cloud + admin; migration 152) · Pull a till's or a branch server's log from the admin portal
Owner, 2026-10-19/20: "add a feature where we can pull local logs of a server or a till to cloud so that we can be
investigating such issues" — and, on the admin portal's Desktop updates tab: "how do I pull logs". Until now (A519) a log
reached support only when someone at the shop pressed "Send logs to support" on the till's Tech page. **BUILT:**
**Cloud** — migration 152 `log_requests` (device, reason, range 24/72/168 h, include `{auth}`, status
waiting/delivered/expired/cancelled, the linked `support_logs` row, expires 7 days on; RLS on, service role only).
`routes/logRequestsAdmin.ts` (mounted at /admin/clients before /admin; any active admin — super admins and agents):
`GET/POST /api/admin/clients/:id/log-requests` and `…/:id/cancel` — the reason required and cleaned, a device of another
business refused (404), retired or not approved (409), 20 per admin per hour (counted in the table), audited in
`admin_audit_log`, a till older than 1.0.20 noted ("this till runs 1.0.5 — it can only send logs from its Tech page from
1.0.18, and answer a pull from 1.0.20"); no owner notice (a support action, as A519). The /admin write hook no longer makes
every till socket sign in again for it (`res.locals.forgetNothing`). `routes/support.ts`: `GET /api/support/log-requests/mine`
(the till's own session, its own waiting requests only) and `POST /api/support/logs` + `request_id` (this business's, THIS
device's, still waiting — else 404/403/409; linked and marked delivered; not counted against A519's 5 an hour). Expiry on
every read (`lib/logRequests.ts expireWaiting`) — no job. **How the till learns:** the doorbell — `liveHub.ringLogRequest`
sends `{type:'log_request', device_id}` to that business's push-channel sockets (A531; the till named asks /mine, others
ignore it) — and the 90 s remote-close beat (A521 `remoteCloseBeat`) asks /mine once, so a till behind a branch server (no
socket of its own; its calls go through the server's gateway, A410, unchanged) or one whose socket is down hears within
~90 s. An older cloud (its 404) is not asked again for an hour. **Till** — `logPull.ts`: A519's bundle (`supportLogs.ts`:
the same redaction, gzip, 900 kB cap) for the request's window, read lazily across the rolled files (`lazyLogFiles`: a file
last written before the window is never opened), up to 3 MB of log text, auth.log only when asked, and a diagnostics block
(version, role, branch, terminal, sync state with what waits per table, failed / parked, cloud reachability, A531 mode /
channel / last change / topics, printer errors in the window, disk free). One upload at a time; a failing upload tried 3
times then left (the request stays waiting); a closed request never again. The shop's log says "logs pulled by ZapTill
support (request …)". **Admin** — `PullLogsCard.tsx` inside the Support logs card (Desktop updates tab): device (label,
role, branch, version, last seen), 24 h / 3 days / 7 days, include sign-in history, reason → Request; the list (waiting with
"till last seen 14:02" and Cancel, delivered with View / Download, expired, cancelled), refreshed every 15 s while one waits.
Tests: `tests/log-requests-a533.test.mjs` (30), `apps/desktop/test/log-pull-a533.test.mjs` (23, a ci.yml step),
`scripts/test-migration-152.mjs` (9) — mutation-checked.

### A532 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-19 (cloud only) · Owner alerts and summaries to more than one person were refused by Resend
Render log, 2026-10-19 (pasted by the owner): `[mailer] Resend error … Invalid \`to\` field` then `[ownerAlerts] not-syncing
alert failed for Pollo Fried Chicken · T1: Connection timeout`, every 15 minutes. The alert jobs and the daily summary join
their recipients into one string ("owner@x, manager@y"); resend 6.33 (Dependabot #72, 2026-10-18) refuses the joined form —
a single recipient (the owner's test email) still went, which is why the e-mail check passed. The SendGrid backup is not
configured (`SENDGRID_API_KEY` unset) and Render filters SMTP 465/587, so nothing reached anyone. **BUILT:** `lib/mailer.ts`
`mailRecipients()` — every Resend send (sendEmail and sendEmailChecked) gets a list, one entry per address; an entry that is
not an address (a phone number or a word saved in an e-mail field) is dropped with one log line so the rest still go; an
empty list throws a clear error. Test `tests/mailer-recipients-a532.test.mjs` (5, mutation-checked against the stand-in
Resend API). **Also seen in the same log, left as they are:** `[tillScope] DRY-RUN would refuse … GET /api/staff` — the
till's whole pull reads staff names with its own sign-in; A415's `TILL_SCOPE_ENFORCE` must stay unset until the till takes
names from its roster (a 1.0.20 follow-up); `SENDGRID_API_KEY` unset (no e-mail backup) — the owner's call.

### A531 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-19 (till 1.0.20 + cloud; migration 151) · Change-triggered sync — a till takes a change when there is one, and only the rows that changed
Owner, 2026-10-19: "this should only happen when there is a change, no need to keep asking for the same item … a change in
menu do this, change in financial settings do this, change in system settings do this. Critical should be instant,
non-critical can take effect after 1 hr or 30 min." Then: "the till does not have to check, the trigger should happen
instantly — if I change fries from 100 to 150 the trigger should only send the affected product and price, not the whole
menu (70 products → 69 needless); if Eugene's PIN changes only Eugene's change gets synced, not all 150 staff." And:
"for a setup like KRUNCH only the server does the communication to cloud, not all tills". Measured after A528 (admin
System page): `/api/pos` 5.0 MB in 36 min across ~4 tills — `syncAll` took the whole `/api/pos/init` (~300 KB, the logo in
base64 included, plus one request per product with options, inventory, staff, tables, pumps, stations) every 10 minutes
whether anything changed or not, and every till asked the version every 20 s and the staff list every 10–20 s.

**BUILT — the cloud:**
- **Migration 151** `public.sync_changes` (seq bigserial, business, branch or null, topic, LOGICAL table, row id, upsert /
  delete, changed_at = clock_timestamp(); index (business_id, seq); RLS on, no policy) written by trigger
  `log_sync_change()` (AFTER, per row, SECURITY DEFINER, never fails the write) on 28 tables. One entry per changed row,
  the same row and operation once per transaction; a part (an option, a combo line, a branch price, a grant) is an upsert
  of what it belongs to; a delete of a product / category / person / table / pump / offer is a delete. Not written: an
  update that changes nothing (updated_at alone), a person merely active (last_active_at, sign-in code fields), a branch's
  tech code / KDS version, a businesses column no till reads, the e-mail jobs' bookkeeping keys. `sync_versions` (150)
  moves exactly as before (old tills), and payment_methods, category_stations and pumps now move the catalogue version
  too (old tills learned of them only on the 10-minute pull). `sync_changes_since(business, since, branch, limit)` (the
  entries after `since` for the branch or every branch, plus the last 120 s — a transaction numbered before another but
  committed after it is not skipped), `sync_changes_heads(after)` (one read for every business), `prune_sync_changes(days)`
  + `sync_change_floor` (30 days kept, a daily 03:17 UTC job; a till behind the floor takes the whole menu once). The
  functions are revoked from PUBLIC / anon / authenticated and granted to service_role. `scripts/schema-pending.json`
  declares 151.
- **Topics** (`shared/syncTopics.ts`, copied to the server and the till; `public.sync_setting_topic` is its SQL mirror —
  the migration test runs both on 43 keys): **menu** (critical) products, categories, variants / add-ons, combos, branch
  prices, offers, promotions, stock counts, the `stock_count_freeze` setting; **staff** (critical) people, their branches,
  grants, roles, role grants; **money** (critical) payment methods, feature_flags (POS switches), businesses VAT / CTL /
  currency / status / web access, and the settings `payment_methods_enabled`, `continuous_operation`,
  `business_day_cutoff`, `cashier_history_methods`, `cashier_sees_shift_sales`, `cashier_history_totals`,
  `cashier_own_history`, `cashier_no_reprint`, `cashier_no_money_out`, `service_charge_pct`, `pay_later_tabs`,
  `pay_before_kitchen`, `etims_enabled`, `default_parking_rate`, any `mpesa_*`, `receipt_pay_*`, `aggregator_commission_*`,
  `parking_rate_*`, `loyalty_*`, `delivery_*`, `void_*`, `offline_*`, `ctl_*`, any key containing `tax` or `vat`;
  **look** (≤ 30 min) business_branding, the `themes` switch, the business name, the settings `thank_you_message`,
  `receipt_*` (header, footer …), `business_*`, `contact_*`; **setup** (≤ 30 min) print stations and their categories,
  tables, pumps, branches, the business type / support tech, every other setting (`kitchen_exclusions`,
  `order_note_picks`, restaurant, fuel, parking options …). Bookkeeping (nothing): `owner_alerts_state`,
  `weekly_summary_last_sent`, `monthly_pack_last_sent`, `report_schedule_last_sent`, `branch_open_tills_last_sent:*`.
- **`GET /api/pos/changes?since=&branch_id=`** (`lib/syncChanges.ts`): the changed rows THEMSELVES, in the shape the till
  already stores from /init (a product with its category name / colour and THIS branch's price, cost removed; a combo's
  lines; a product's variant and add-on groups; categories; offers and promotions as offers; the branch's stock-count
  freeze; a person's users row and roster row — exactly as branch-staff makes it, bcrypt only, never the override PIN,
  and only to a till's own session; `config` money / look / setup = that topic's handful of init keys; `branding`; the
  print-station list; tables and pumps at this branch) or a delete marker. The newest entry per row; another branch's
  rows never (the entry's branch, and the row's own); every read by the caller's business (another business's id in an
  entry is a delete marker — nothing leaks). 500 a page + `more`; `full_resync_needed` behind the floor; without `since`:
  where the log is. The answer is shared 5 s per (business, branch, since, till?, sees costs?). 404
  `CHANGES_UNAVAILABLE` before 151 (the till keeps its old way), 503 on a read error.
- **Push channel** `/api/pos/live` (`lib/liveHub.ts`, the `ws` package already a dependency, the same port): the first
  message `{type:'hello', token}` within 10 s, checked by the same `requireAuth` (a bad / expired token, a blocked or
  retired till: 4001; a person's or web session: 4003; never in the URL); the upgrade answer signed `X-ZapTill-Server`
  (A529); `ready {last_seq}`; ping every 45 s; closed at the token's expiry (+60 s) and whenever a write here touches the
  business's tills (forgetOnWrite `tills`); re-checked every 10 min. A write through this server (every forgetOnWrite
  router) rings the business's sockets ~300 ms later (one read of its newest entry); anything else (the SQL editor, a
  migration) on ONE `sync_changes_heads` read for every business every 5 s, only while a socket is open. In memory — one
  instance (WEB_CONCURRENCY=1); a second instance would need a shared channel. The push is a doorbell: what changed is
  always read from /changes.
- **Compression** (`lib/compressJson.ts`, zlib, no new dependency — `compression` streams without Content-Length, and
  A528's traffic counter reads that header): a JSON answer of 1 KB or more is gzip (or deflate) for a client that accepts
  it, sent with its real length; never a HEAD, a 204 / 304, an already-encoded answer, a redirect or anything streamed,
  never `/api/desktop-update/*`. Node's fetch unpacks it; the branch gateway already drops Content-Encoding.
- **/init built once per catalogue version** (`lib/posInit.ts`; `routes/pos.ts` buildInit — the reads and rules moved
  unchanged): kept per (business, requested branch, version) — 200 answers / 50 MB, LRU, 10 minutes at most, version 0
  never; two tills at once share one build. Nothing per caller in it (checked: no token, device, person or permission is
  read); the licence gate and the cost prices are applied per request, after. `/changes` answers config / branding from
  it, rebuilt when it is older than the change (+3 s for the two clocks).

**BUILT — the till** (`apps/desktop/src/main/liveSync.ts`). **Direct** (no branch server, or the branch server itself):
ONE socket; on `changed` (or `ready` past its number) one `/changes?since=`, and the rows are written with the SAME helpers
the whole pull uses (`syncEngine.ts`: pullCatalogue's transaction split into writeCategories / writeProducts /
writeComboItems (per combo) / writeChoices (per product) / writeOffers + putOffer / writeStations / writeUsers /
writeTables / writePumps (per row) / writeStockLevels; `applyChangeEntries`; a product or category delete → status
'inactive', an offer / table / pump delete → gone; a staff row → `branchStaff.applyBranchStaffChanges`, one person, their
saved sign-ins follow). Menu / staff / money at once; look / setup kept on disk and applied when no drawer is open (a
server: none in the branch), at a shift opening or closing, or after 30 min — never with a cart, the payment screen open
or a print pending (activityTracker). No timer asks anything while the socket is up (the 10-minute `syncAll` skips the
catalogue — its pushes, tech config, day-close and test-clear checks stay); socket down → reconnect 5 s → 5 min and
`/changes` every 5 min (20 s with a drawer open or a sale in the last 5 min). The whole catalogue at first start (the
log's number first), on `full_resync_needed`, and once a day (the safety pull, never mid-sale). Stock levels (sales move
them; the log does not carry sales) re-read every 30 min when stock is tracked. **Branch server**: logs what it applied
into SQLite `live_log` (its own order; a staff row without its PIN hash) and serves `GET /node/live?since=` (a proven
till only; the PIN hash from its own list; `full_resync_needed` after its own resync or the 7-day prune; 404 while it is
itself on the old way). **Peer**: never asks the cloud for changes, the menu, the staff list or a version — `/node/live`
every 20 s on the LAN; the A448 local change counter rides along; the roster timer (A446) stands down to a 30-minute
safety, the server's copy first. **Old cloud / old server** (their own signed 404): today's behaviour, asked again hourly.
One log line per topic applied (rows, tables, change number, bytes); the Tech page shows the channel, what waits, each
topic's last change and the last whole catalogue. The whole pull also stops re-applying pending stock deductions over
levels it did not refresh (they were taken off twice when the stock read failed).

**Bytes, measured in the tests:** fries 100 → 150 = 421 bytes on the wire (one product row; the ring a ~60-byte frame);
Eugene's PIN = 574 bytes (his row only). A 70-product test menu's /init: 21.8 KB of JSON, 1.6 KB gzip.
**Estimate per till per hour, nothing changing** (catalogue and staff traffic only): before ≈ 180 version checks + 180
staff-list asks (360 on a server) + 6 whole pulls (6 × (6 + products with options) requests, ≈ 6 × 300 KB) ≈ 370+
requests and ≈ 2 MB (the measured 5.0 MB / 36 min / 4 tills ≈ 2.1 MB). After: 1 socket (≈ 4 reconnects at the token
renewal, ≈ 80 pings), 2 staff-list safety asks, ≤ 2 stock reads, 1/24 of a whole pull ≈ 8 requests and ≈ 10–60 KB.
**A 4-till branch with a server**: before ≈ 1,500 requests and ≈ 8.4 MB an hour from 4 machines; after ≈ 8 requests and
≈ 10–60 KB from the server only; the 3 tills ask the server on the LAN. Per change: one ring and one /changes per direct
machine (one per branch).
**Left as they are (said):** each peer's other polls still go through the server's gateway one by one — web sales on its
drawers, shift states, confirmations (20 s, only while it has a drawer open or a close waiting), the 90 s remote-close /
test-clear beat, and the 10-minute pushes / tech config / day-close checks: answering them from one branch-level poll
needs a per-drawer contract on the server and the cloud — not simple; A528's caches keep them cheap. Not row-level:
`config` (a setting sends its topic's keys, ~10–20 values — several init values are derived from several settings: the
M-Pesa line, the reversal rules), the print-station list (a few rows, replaced whole as the till always has), the stock
count (the branch's freeze list), stock levels (re-read every 30 min). The upgrade answer is signed, but a till cannot
read upgrade headers through the WebSocket API — the push is only a doorbell; the data comes through `/changes`, judged as
every answer (A529). Tests: `scripts/test-migration-151.mjs` (23), `tests/sync-changes-a531.test.mjs` (24),
`apps/desktop/test/live-sync-a531.test.mjs` (25, ci step "Desktop change-triggered sync (A531)"), each mutation-checked.

### A530 · P2 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-19 (till 1.0.20 + web POS + admin) · The receipt used too much paper — the compact receipt is the standard, four classic switches per client
Owner, 2026-10-19: "I feel the receipt is too long wasting paper" — all four changes agreed as the standard, and "the
switch settings … should be in the admin per client". Measured: ESC 2 (1/6", ~34 dots) for a 24-dot glyph; a logo up to
384 x 288 dots (36 mm); 3 lines fed before a GS V 66 0 that already feeds to the blade; the sample receipt 46 lines with
11 rules. **BUILT** (shared/printing, so the till and the web POS print the same; kitchen, dispatch and the Z-report
unchanged, byte for byte):
- **Layout** (`render.ts` renderReceipt): 5 rules (under the header, the item heading, the items, before PAY, before the
  closing block); Type + Bill No. on one line ("Type: " dropped where it does not fit, 58 mm); Cashier + time on one line
  (the full stamp on 80 mm, "05/08/26 19:42" on 58 mm, stacked under a long name); no Kots line; Round Off only when not
  0.00; no Total line when there is no tip and no delivery fee (PAY is the total); no "Payment Detail:" heading; the owner's
  box runs into the closing block; a Voided line wraps on 58 mm. Kept: name, branch, header lines, PIN, Tel, every item
  and option and note, offers/discount, SubTotal, CTL (when levied), VAT, PAY, payments, CHANGE, the M-Pesa line, the
  thank-you, TAX RECEIPT UPON REQUEST (when VAT applies), the credit; the Duplicate/VOID/BILL banners.
- **Spacing** (`escpos.ts`, `Document.lineSpacing`): ESC 3 26 (~3.25 mm) for normal-size lines; a double-height line
  (PAY, a banner) keeps ESC 2; ESC 2 is restored at the end of the job.
- **Logo** (`raster.ts`): STORED full size as before (up to 288 dots, 36 mm — `RECEIPT_LOGO_MAX_HEIGHT`, the till's
  `brandingGuard` RGBA_MAX_HEIGHT and `prepareRasterLogo` RECEIPT_MAX_H unchanged; owner, 2026-10-19: "that's okay", so
  `receipt_full_logo` works for every logo, old or new) and PRINTED at most 120 dots (15 mm,
  `RECEIPT_LOGO_PRINT_MAX_HEIGHT`), shrunk at print time by `fitMonoRaster` — area sampling, black at >= 40% ink so a
  2-dot stroke survives at any position (nearest neighbour loses it). The web Branding preview shows the printed 15 mm
  ("full size if ZapTill turns on Full-size logo").
- **Feed** (`Document.cutFeed`): 1 line before the cut when the printer cuts; 3 on a tear-off printer (no cut).
- **Switches** (`shared/posFeatures.ts`, every copy; off = compact): `receipt_classic_spacing`, `receipt_full_logo`,
  `receipt_classic_layout`, `receipt_extra_feed`, mapped by `receiptClassicFrom` to `BusinessConfig.receiptClassic`. Set in
  the admin portal (Features › "Receipt (classic switches)", toggles — not an owner option; the client's PUT /api/flags
  refuses them as every POS switch). They reach the till and the web POS with pos/init `posFeatures`: the till's receipt
  queue (`ipcHandlers` queueThermal, from `getPosFeatures()`) and its test print/preview (`printWorker`); the web POS's
  receipt (`PaymentModal`), Print Bill (`printRouted`) and the web reprint (`reprintReceipt`, GET /api/flags).
All four on = the 1.0.19 receipt byte for byte: `shared/printing/test/golden/a530-classic.json` (26 receipts — tip, fee,
free delivery, offer, dine-in, proforma, duplicate, void, a 288-dot logo, round-off, zero-rated, a long name; 80 and
58 mm) was written by the 1.0.19 renderer. Sample (SAMPLE-OUTPUT.txt, before/after section): 46 -> 34 lines; estimated
210 -> 118 mm on 80 and 58 mm, 246 -> 133 mm with a 288-dot logo (~44-46% less paper). Tests
`shared/printing/test/receipt-compact.test.ts` (163, mutation-checked) and `tests/receipt-compact-a530.test.mjs` (6).
**Open (why P2 stays open):** ESC 3 n counts the printer's vertical motion unit — 1/203" on the 203 dpi heads we target
(XP-80 class), but some Epson models use 1/360", where 26 would be ~1.8 mm and the lines would overlap: prove on paper on
each printer model; `receipt_classic_spacing` is that client's way back. The till's HTML receipt (a Windows printer, not
thermal ESC/POS) is unchanged. A logo shrunk from its stored 1-bit form is a shade bolder than one fitted from colour.
**2026-10-21 — A538 changed the standard** (owner, on paper: "it feels congested everywhere … top arrangement totally
off"; chose "go back to the old layout", "line spacing in the middle, about 3.75 mm"): the classic layout is the standard
again at ESC 3 30 (~3.75 mm), keeping this item's small printed logo and 1-line feed; the compact layout above is an
opt-in (`receipt_compact_layout`); `receipt_classic_layout` is retired (a stored row is ignored, no migration). The
golden promise now reads: classic spacing + full logo + extra feed on = 1.0.19 byte for byte. See A538.

### A529 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-19 (till 1.0.20 + cloud) · A cloud that answers with someone else's page is UNREACHABLE (sign-in falls back, sales never 'failed')
During the Render suspension (A528) the owner reported: "some users were not able to log in … and I thought we had said
when the desktop is offline or render unavailable all users should be able to log in", and "the could not sync error some
clients did not like it". Root: the till fell back to its own staff list / saved sign-ins only on a THROWN fetch, a 5xx
(A152 `isUnreachableStatus`), a 429 or a 401 session refusal. A suspended Render service, a Cloudflare error page or a
captive portal answers with ITS OWN page (404, 403, 410, 200 HTML) — read as the cloud's verdict: "Invalid PIN" at the PIN
pad; every sale pushed into it counted an attempt and went 'failed' after 5 (red "N sales failed to sync" for managers
though the sales were safe); a void/refund was refused (only 502/503/504 went offline); a renewal answered by such a page
could be read as a refusal (session held 15 min, device sign-in tried). The A446 re-queue matched only certain texts.

**BUILT:**
- **Cloud** (`lib/serverSignature.ts`, first in `index.ts`'s chain so nothing can skip it): every answer carries
  `X-ZapTill-Server: 1` — routes, an unknown route's 404, the error handler's 500, a CORS 403, the limiters' 429, /health.
  Not a secret: it says who answered.
- **One rule in the till** (`authTransport.ts` `fromOurCloud` / `judgeCloudAnswer`, applied in `cloudGateway.ts`
  `cloudFetch` — the one door every cloud call goes through: sign-in and unlock, sync push/pull (orders, shifts, days,
  floats, expenses, kitchen voids, confirmations, prices, wastage, station categories, branding, changes, the staff list,
  day-close acks), renewals and the device sign-in, void/refund, manager screens, tech config, branch report, update
  checks): an answer to the cloud's address WITHOUT the signature throws `ForeignPageError` ("fetch failed: the cloud did
  not answer (another server's page, HTTP 404)") — exactly no connection, whatever its status: sign-in falls back to the
  till's own staff list / saved sign-ins; a push stays pending, no attempt counted; a renewal "could not reach" (tokens
  kept, never a refusal, no device sign-in); a void/refund goes `reverseWhileOffline`; a manager screen says "No
  connection". A 5xx WITH the signature keeps A152; a 4xx WITH it is a real answer (a wrong PIN stays final).
- **Backward compatibility**: the rule applies only once THIS cloud (its origin) has been seen to sign an answer; until
  then an unsigned answer is judged by today's status rules (a 1.0.20 till on a cloud before A529 = 1.0.19). "Seen to
  sign" is kept on disk (`maintenance_state` `cloud_signs:<origin>`), so a till restarted DURING an outage still knows.
  A cloud rolled back below A529 is recognised by an unsigned 2xx JSON answer (a portal / suspended page is HTML): the
  till forgets and today's rules apply until it signs again. The update files (the cloud redirects them to GitHub) are
  exempt when 2xx (sha512-checked against the cloud's latest.yml).
- **Branch server**: the gateway passes `X-ZapTill-Server` through unchanged (a peer judges the forwarded answer the same
  way); its own `X-Node-Uplink: down` 502 is unchanged; the renewal it brokers for a peer goes through `cloudFetch` (a
  foreign page → 503, the peer keeps its sign-in).
- **Recovery**: sales left 'failed' by the line are re-queued at the start of a push whenever the cloud has answered again
  (also when every waiting sale had gone 'failed' — before, only after a pushed sale); the A446 match now includes "another
  server's page" and a bare "HTTP nnn" (what an earlier build stored for a page with no JSON error — our cloud always words
  its refusals). Until then they count as WAITING, not failed (`getSyncStatus`).
- **Wording** (`renderer/lib/syncNotice.ts`): the outage is the quiet notice — "N records waiting to sync · the cloud cannot
  be reached · last synced …"; red only for a refusal by our cloud. Cashiers still see nothing (A363).
- **Logs**: one line per fallback naming the status and that the page was not the cloud's ('pin' at sign-in, 'sale' for a
  void/refund, 'manage', and 'sync' from cloudFetch at most once a minute per status); learning / forgetting the signature
  is logged.
- **Options on every tap** (the owner's System page, 2026-10-19: `/api/variants` 557 calls in 36 min across ~4 tills):
  `pos:getVariants` / `pos:getModifiers` asked the cloud whenever a product had no local option groups — nearly every tap
  (most products have none), and a slow or down cloud held the item up to 15 s before the cart. Now an empty local list
  after a catalogue pull means no options (the products table is written only by a pull — the marker); only a till that
  has never pulled asks, bounded to 2 s, and a foreign page there is no connection (empty). Edge: a product whose choices
  failed to arrive in a till's very first pull shows none until the next pull (A425 keeps what a product had).
- **Deliberately left**: the install screen's connection test (plain /health before enrolment — any answer = reachable);
  the till's calls to its own branch server (`/node/*`, the server's own answers, A501).

**Tests**: `apps/desktop/test/foreign-page-a529.test.mjs` (30; real dist/main, real SQLite, stand-in cloud; 9 mutations
bite — the `isTransportError` name is belt and braces, the "fetch failed" text matches too); `tests/server-signature-a529.test.mjs`
(6; the compiled server run as deployed: route, /health 503, unknown 404, thrown 500, CORS 403, the sign-in limiter's 429;
2 mutations bite). CI: a desktop step; the root suite runs it.

### A528 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-19 (cloud only; migration 150) · The cloud's polling cost suspended production
Render suspended production on 2026-10-19: its 5 GB "Included Bandwidth" was 6.29 GB — 5 GB "Service-Initiated" (the
server's own requests to Supabase) and 1.29 GB answers; Supabase was at 5.53/5 GB egress and 7.54/1 GB log ingestion (one
log line per PostgREST request). Root: every till asked `GET /api/pos/catalogue-version` every 20 s and each answer ran
**16 queries** (the newest updated_at of 16 tables); every till request also read its user_devices row (a person's: the
users row, an owner-role PIN sign-in also businesses.owner_id); `/api/pos/branch-staff` (20 s per till, 10 s on a branch
server) read the device row and the whole staff list with roles and grants on EVERY ask, deciding "unchanged" only after
the read; every answer carried ~1.2 KB of helmet document headers. Owner, 2026-10-19: "can we do it such that only a
change can trigger data sync … we need a solution and a quick one". **Part A (this entry) is the cloud alone** — live when
it reaches main, for every till version in the field; Part B (tills and the branch server asking by change) is a later
desktop build.

**BUILT:**
- **Migration 150** `public.sync_versions` (business_id, topic, version, updated_at; RLS on, no policy). Trigger
  `bump_sync_version(topic)` (SECURITY DEFINER, AFTER, per row) on the 16 catalogue tables → topic `catalogue`; on users,
  roles, role_permissions, user_branches, user_permissions and user_devices (only when status, retired_at, branch_id,
  business_id or device_role change — not last_seen_at / last_sync_at) → topic `staff`. The business is the row's
  business_id, else through its branch / role / person; businesses by its own id. Once per business and topic per
  transaction (a transaction-local flag: a 2,000-product import bumps once). The e-mail jobs' bookkeeping rows in
  business_settings (owner_alerts_state every 15 min, weekly/monthly/report last-sent, branch_open_tills_last_sent:*) do
  not bump — they used to move the old version and make every till pull. Never fails the write that fired it (a
  warning). A missing table is skipped (to_regclass). Seeded: every business, both topics, version 1.
- **catalogue-version** answers `{ version: "cv:<n>" }` from ONE row, remembered 15 s per business (`lib/syncVersions.ts`)
  — one query per business per 15 s however many tills. Tills compare it for equality only (`syncEngine.ts`
  pullIfCatalogueChanged), so each till pulls ONCE on the new format (and once more when migration 150 lands if the server
  deployed first). A branch row bumps its business: a printer changed at one branch makes the business's other tills pull
  once. **Fallback** (the table missing — Render and the db-migrate job run in parallel on a merge — or the read failing):
  the 16 reads as before, remembered 60 s per business and branch; a null answer is never kept.
- **branch-staff**: the staff version is read BEFORE the list; when it has not moved since this branch's last answer and the
  till holds that answer (`?v=`), it is told "unchanged" with no read (the same `{ branch_id, version, unchanged: true }`
  every till since 1.0.15 already handles). A full re-read at least every 10 minutes per branch. Before migration 150: read
  every time, as before. The device row comes from the sign-in check's cache.
- **requireAuth** remembers 30 s (`lib/authCache.ts`, 5,000 entries per map): the till's user_devices row, the person's users
  row, businesses.owner_id, and the Supabase session's owner role. Only a row that lets the request in is kept — a refusal,
  a missing row and a failed read never (a rejoined till or a reactivated person is let in at once; a failed read still
  503s). A token NEWER than the remembered row (renewed after a change) is read again, never refused in a renewal loop.
  **Forgotten at once** on any non-GET request on `/devices`, `/tills-days` (tills), `/staff`, `/changes` (people + staff
  + catalogue), `/business`, `/controls` (owner, people), `/admin/*` (every business), and in `deviceBinding.ts` (a till
  bound or moved) and `/auth/enrol/redeem` (a till rejoined) — `lib/forgetOnWrite.ts`, `routes/index.ts`. Catalogue routes
  (products, categories, variants, modifiers, combos, business, controls, flags, tables, branches, printers, stations,
  branch-prices, stock-takes, offers, promotions, onboarding, payment-methods) drop the catalogue version at once.
  **A change made directly in SQL (or the Supabase dashboard) takes up to 30 s for the sign-in check, 15 s for the
  versions.** A till's own push (`/api/sync/push`) and a legacy PIN hash upgraded at verify-pin reach the versions through
  the trigger, within 15 s.
- **Headers** (`lib/apiHeaders.ts`): this server serves JSON and CSV/spreadsheet downloads only (no HTML route). Dropped
  content-security-policy, cross-origin-opener-policy, origin-agent-cluster, x-dns-prefetch-control, x-download-options,
  x-permitted-cross-domain-policies, x-xss-protection; kept strict-transport-security, x-content-type-options,
  cross-origin-resource-policy (cross-origin), referrer-policy, x-frame-options. **Compression is NOT on**: `compression`
  is not a dependency of the server — not added here; a later decision.
- **Measured**: `lib/trafficStats.ts` counts requests and bytes per route family since start, the catalogue-version and
  sign-in hit rates, branch-staff full vs unchanged, and the database queries of the polled paths —
  `GET /api/admin/ops/summary` `traffic` (super admins only) and a "Traffic since start" card on the admin portal's System
  page.

**Expected (from the code, per till per minute, polled paths):** before ≈ 48 (catalogue-version 3 × 16) + 6 (branch-staff 3
× device + list; 12 on a branch server) + ~13 sign-in reads (catalogue-version, branch-staff, shifts/state, web sales pull 3
each, close beat, update ask) ≈ **67 queries per till per minute**, the staff list with its roles and grants the heaviest
answer. After ≈ **2 per till** (its device row every 30 s) **+ ~8 per business** (the two versions every 15 s, shared by
every till), the staff list only when staff change. A 3-till business: ~200 → ~14 a minute. Answers ~1 KB lighter each.

Tests `tests/polling-cost-a528.test.mjs` (27, mutation-checked — 11 mutations, each bites) and
`scripts/test-migration-150.mjs` (30, PGlite over every migration — 7 mutations, each bites).

### A527 · P2 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-17 (till 1.0.19 + cloud + web) · A manager confirming a shift saw one expected cash figure, not what it is made of
Owner, 2026-10-17: "a manager when closing should see 4 items — 1. opening float, 2. cash sold, 3. cash sold + float,
4. what the cashier keyed in". **BUILT:** the confirm screens show the cash as Opening float · Cash sold · Cash sold +
float · Cashier keyed in, above the counts — the till's Confirm shift (`ConfirmShiftModal`), the branch server's Close
Branch confirm (`BranchCloseTab`), and the web's Shift confirmations (manager portal Shifts tab, owner's Open shifts). One
list for every screen (`shared/shiftConfirm.ts` `cashLines`). When cash was put in or taken out, or paid as a cash
expense, two more lines show it and the drawer's expected cash, so the lines always add up to what the difference is
measured against (`other` is derived from expected, never summed separately). Sent with the expected figures only —
to a manager signed in on the till (the IPC drops it otherwise) or someone who may confirm on the cloud
(`/api/shifts/:id/confirm-view` `cash`); a cashier holding the screen, or a manager typing a PIN on it, sees none. The
cashier's figure is shown to that manager even without 'confirm_shows_cashier_figures' (the owner's ask); reasons are
still asked only with that switch. A till before 1.0.19 sends no cashier figure to Close Branch — the line is left out
there, not read as "not keyed in". Tests `tests/manager-cash-lines-a527.test.mjs` (15, mutation-checked) and
`apps/desktop/test/shift-confirm.test.mjs` (the till's real confirm view).

### A525 · P2 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-17 (cloud + admin + GitHub; migration 149) · A failed deploy and known vulnerabilities went unnoticed — now checked, recorded and shown in the admin portal
Production (`api.zaptill.co.ke`) silently failed EVERY deploy from 1.0.16 to 1.0.18: a startup guard refused
MPESA_ENVIRONMENT=sandbox with NODE_ENV=production, Render kept the old 1.0.15 instance running, and nobody noticed for two
releases; `npm audit` showed 7 vulnerabilities nobody was told about. Owner, 2026-10-17: "how can I be logging such, like
failed deployment, such vulnerabilities and how to fix them" … "maybe can we have a UI for all that in the app, these
results are written to the db and I can read through". **BUILT:** **Cloud** — `/health` carries `commit` (12 characters of
Render's RENDER_GIT_COMMIT, or null) and `started_at`, in the 200 and the 503 answer (`lib/opsEvents.ts buildInfo`). The
server records its own start after it listens (`recordBoot`: a `boot` row, never awaited, never throws, a missing table is a
warning; skipped under NODE_ENV=test). `public.ops_events` (migration 149: kind boot / deploy_check / vuln_scan, status ok /
warn / fail, commit, title, details jsonb, source; RLS on, no policy). `POST /api/ops/events` (`routes/ops.ts`) for the GitHub
workflows: `Authorization: Bearer` compared in constant time to the new optional env `OPS_INGEST_TOKEN` (at least 32
characters; unset or short = 503 OPS_INGEST_DISABLED, wrong = 401), 60 per address per 10 minutes on top of the global
limiter, zod-checked (deploy_check / vuln_scan only — `boot` comes only from the server; details at most 64 KB); a `fail`
tells the ZapTill admin through the watchdog's channel (`notifyAdmin`, Telegram and e-mail), best effort. **Admin** — super
admins only (`routes/opsAdmin.ts`, requireSuperAdmin; agents refused): `GET /api/admin/ops/events` (kind / status filter,
newest first, a page at a time with the total) and `/summary` (the latest start, deploy check and scan, and what runs now).
A "System" page in the menu (`SystemPage.tsx`, hidden from agents): Production server (the commit it runs, since when, the
last start), Last deploy check (expected against running, the "what to do" of a failure, the GitHub run), Dependencies
(critical / high / moderate / low per app), then the history with a kind filter and expandable details — for a scan each
vulnerable package: app, severity, affected range, the fix (and whether it is a major upgrade), advisories with links.
**GitHub** — `.github/workflows/verify-prod-deploy.yml` (push to main + manual): the newest commit touching `apps/server` or
`render.yaml` (Render with a rootDir redeploys only then) must be an ancestor of the commit `/health` names, polled every 30 s
for 20 minutes; ok → a deploy_check ok event; still old (or no `commit` — an older server) → a deploy_check fail event with
what to do, and the job fails so GitHub e-mails too. `.github/workflows/security-scan.yml` (daily 05:00 UTC + push to main +
manual): `npm audit --package-lock-only` (no install) in server (`--omit=dev`), dashboard, admin, desktop and the root, one
vuln_scan event built by `scripts/ops-audit-summary.mjs` (fail = a high or critical in the server, warn = anything else, ok =
nothing; the job fails only when a scan could not run). `ci.yml`: "Server dependency audit" (`npm audit --omit=dev
--audit-level=high --package-lock-only` in apps/server — 0 after the nodemailer 10.0.16 upgrade) and the summary's
self-test. `.github/dependabot.yml`: npm for the four apps and the root plus github-actions, weekly, target `dev`, at most 5
open, minor and patch grouped per directory. Tests: `tests/ops-events-a525.test.mjs` (22), `scripts/test-migration-149.mjs`
(8), `ops-audit-summary.mjs --self-test` (6). **Owner setup:** the same token (`node -e
"console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('hex'))"`) as `OPS_INGEST_TOKEN` on Render (production service →
Environment) and as a GitHub repository secret; Dependabot alerts and security updates on; Render's failed-deploy e-mails on.
Found by the first scan (warn, not the server): dashboard 8 high, admin 2 high, desktop 2 critical and 16 high — build tools
mostly (tailwind 3 → 4, electron-builder majors), to be worked through from the System page.

### A523 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-17 (till 1.0.18 + cloud + web + admin; no migration) · Simple day-to-day closes without back and forth: empty days close themselves; the owner and support close a till's day or drawer from the cloud
Owner, 2026-10-17: "I don't want this back and forth, clients not being able to do simple tasks day to day operations, to
make it worse there is no location on the cloud where I can close day as the owner or tech support remote force close."
Chose all three; "super admins and agents" may rescue. **BUILT:** **Till** — an old trading day with no drawer open and every
shift confirmed (or none) closes itself at the day gate (`dayService.autoCloseEmptyDay`): the confirmed shifts' cash (A452),
`closed_by` NULL, "Closed automatically — nothing left to count", logged and pushed; the next day starts with no manager.
Money (an open drawer, a shift to confirm) still locks, with A520's text. A force-closed (`closed_unreconciled`) drawer does
not hold the day; its expected cash shows as a shortfall. A till learns what the cloud closed before it decides it is locked
(`learnCloudCloses`: web drawer closes → confirmations → waiting day closes) at start-up before the push, at the day gate (at
most once a minute, 8 s cap) and on the 90 s beat. The day-close ack carries `code` (DRAWER_OPEN / SHIFTS_UNCONFIRMED) and
`wait`. **Cloud** — "Tills & days" (`lib/tillsDays.ts`, `routes/tills-days.ts`): one overview per till (version, last sync,
open day, drawers with expected so far for those who may see figures, shifts to confirm, waiting closes, retired/silent).
Close day takes effect on the cloud at once (`business_days` closed, a `cloud_closed` close queued for the till to adopt); a
drawer open refuses unless "force-close the open drawer first" is ticked; a shift to confirm refuses. Also force-close or
count-close a drawer, withdraw a stuck close (never a web close), close as abandoned. Each needs a reason and a tick for a
silent till, is audited, and the owner is told. One close, never two (`mergeCloudClosedDays` in the sync push): the till's
open push never reopens a web-closed day it has not adopted; its close keeps the web's time and closer with its own figures.
A522's abandon queues the same kind of close. **Web** — Finance › Tills & Days for the owner; the manager portal's Shifts tab
for holders of `shifts.close_day` / `shifts.force_close` (their branch). **Admin** — a "Tills & days" tab on the client page
(`routes/tillsDaysAdmin.ts`, any active admin): reason, admin audit plus audit_log, the owner e-mailed, super admins asked to
verify an agent's action, 30 actions per 10 min per admin. Tests `apps/desktop/test/self-closing-days-a523.test.mjs` (37),
`tests/tills-and-days-a523.test.mjs` (30), both mutation-checked; `tests/day-close-till.test.mjs` updated for A521. Owner
action: none (no migration); deploy the cloud with the 1.0.18 tills.

### A509 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-16 (till 1.0.16) · Windows asked for permission at every update — a safe elevated updater task
A508's limit: the installer is per machine and unsigned, so electron-updater ran it through elevate.exe and Windows showed a
UAC prompt at every update; on an unattended till nobody answers it, so the idle install refused. Owner: "Safe updater task,
now". **BUILT:** the installer (already elevated, `build/installer.nsh`, prod flavour only) writes
`updater/zaptill-update.ps1` from its own payload into `%ProgramFiles%\ZapTill Updater` (owner Administrators; SYSTEM and
Administrators write, Users read; `request\` the one folder users write) and registers **ZapTill Updater** (SYSTEM, highest,
no trigger, `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File <that script>`, no arguments; security descriptor
`D:P(A;;FA;;;SY)(A;;FA;;;BA)(A;;GRGX;;;AU)` — users may run it, not change it) and **ZapTill Relaunch** (the INTERACTIVE
group, least privilege: ZapTill.exe in the user's session, never SYSTEM); both deleted on a real uninstall (not on the
uninstall an update runs). The app (`src/main/updaterTask.ts`) only writes `request\update-request.json` {id, version,
installerPath, relaunch}, runs the task and waits for its answer (`updater-status.json`). The script trusts none of it: plain
version, newer than the installed ZapTill.exe's own file version (no downgrade, no re-install), the install folder not
writable by users (the old uninstaller runs from it), a plain local path (no UNC, `..`, stream, link), latest.yml for that
version read over HTTPS (TLS 1.2+, certificates checked) from `github.com/oweyahillary/swiftpos/releases/download/v<version>/`,
the installer copied into `work\` (SYSTEM + Administrators only, made afresh) and THAT copy's SHA-512 and size checked; then
"ready", it waits for ZapTill to close, runs the copy `--updated /S` (TEMP inside `work\`; never `--force-run`), and starts
ZapTill through the relaunch task. The idle install (A508), "Install now" and install-on-close all go through the task;
ZapTill closes only after "ready" — a refusal (offline, behind a branch server without internet, a policy, antivirus) or no
answer in time leaves it running and the update installs on close the old way (elevate.exe, Windows' prompt); the idle
install does not ask again for 6 h. Machines installed before 1.0.16 have no task until they install once more. The Tech
page shows whether the task is there and the tail of `updater.log`. Test `apps/desktop/test/updater-task-a509.test.mjs` (67;
the PowerShell cases run for real on Windows in a test mode that never installs; mutation-checked).
**Limits (open):** a signed-in user can END the running task (Task Scheduler gives "end" with "run") — an install cut off is
an outage, not an elevation; a user can install an official newer release the cloud has not yet approved for the business
(the script cannot ask the cloud — it has no token); the repository must stay public for the SYSTEM fetch (else: install on
close, as before); with Windows Developer Mode on, a user could swap a folder in the installer path for a symbolic link
between the script's link check and its open (the hash still decides what runs).

### A508 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-16 (till 1.0.16) · Tills and servers only updated when someone was there — usage-aware silent install

server's branch copy ready (A496), not busy (cart, payment, printing), idle ≥ 20 min in a quiet hour or ≥ 90 min any time,
or after 72 h idle ≥ 10 min in a quiet hour; then one sync push, the server stops serving, `quitAndInstall(silent, run
after)` — back at the PIN screen, the drawer untouched; the Tech page says when and why (no cashier banner). Test
`apps/desktop/test/silent-update-a508.test.mjs` (71, mutation-checked).
**Limit (open):** the installer is per-machine and unsigned, so Windows asks for administrator permission (UAC) at every
update — the silent install goes ahead only where Windows will not ask; elsewhere it installs on close as before, and the
Tech page says so. Silent installs start from 1.0.16 (1.0.15 installs 1.0.16 the old way). → A509: the updater task.

### A501 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-15 (till 1.0.16) · Tills and the branch server stopped syncing and nothing said why
Owner, 2026-10-15: "their exists a problem beteen a node and and a server syncing you need to look into it and fix it once
and for all … some tills are misbehaving and clients are not happy". Beyond the bill-number clash (A500): a till re-bound to
another branch failed its whole outbox on the server's 403 and only a new address re-armed it; a refused peer row was skipped
for ever (a new trading day arriving with the event that closes the last); a pinned server answering plain still read
"encrypted" and every call failed until a manual re-trust; pinnedFetch built a new pool per request (no cap, a handshake
every call); a server whose address changed (DHCP, port fallback) was lost with the cloud behind it; COALESCE(device_id,'')
defeated the (device_id, seq) indexes; nothing on screen said any of it.
**BUILT:** 400/403/426 from `/node/sync` are transport (rows wait, no attempt counted); a server identity key (pinned code,
server device id, this till's branch) re-arms refused rows when it changes; `peer_quarantine` keeps refused peer rows and
retries them (after the event sweep in the same pass, then backoff 30 s–1 h, 12 attempts), the server retries after its
sweep too; `tls_failed` state, re-checked by itself every 60 s; one pinned agent per certificate, separate pools for the
gateway (16) and the LAN (8); `nodeFollow.ts` follows the till's OWN server to a new address only when the beacon's code,
the certificate byte for byte, an encrypted /node/health and the server's device id all match; `nodeHealth.ts` per-channel
health and the backlog on Tech › Branch sync, with "Retry failed records"; the manager's notice names the real refusal;
queries use the indexes (EXPLAIN-checked); `/node/health` names its protocol and an older server says "Update the branch
server". Test `apps/desktop/test/sync-self-heal.test.mjs` (80, mutation-checked).

### A500 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-15 (till 1.0.16) · A bill number clash refused a sale, or kept it off the branch for ever
Owner, 2026-10-15, a till's log: "distribution: refused 1 orders row(s) from 8bc3b348 and moved on … UNIQUE constraint
failed: orders.order_number", bills printed "T3--5". A bill number is `<terminal code>--<counter>`; a reinstalled till gets
its old code back (A182) under a new device id with the counter at 0, while the server and the other tills still hold its
earlier "T3--1…". The local `orders.order_number` is UNIQUE, so a till pulling from the server skipped the other till's sale
for good (its cursor moves past refused rows), the server failed the till's outbox row after 5 tries, and once the old rows
reached the reinstalled till its own next sale could not be saved at all. (The cloud was already right: migration 94.)
**BUILT:** `main/billNumber.ts` — `nextBillNumber` carries on past the highest `<code>--<n>` held here; a replica arriving
with a number another row holds is stored as `<n>~<device8>` (identity stays the id; the cloud keeps the real number);
a sale rung here keeps its number (on the kitchen ticket already) and a replica holding it is renamed on this machine only.
`repairBillNumberRefusals` runs once per machine: sales refused or skipped before this build are offered and pulled again.
Also: the cloud answers `/api/health` (every till logged "connection test: HTTP 404" through its server's gateway).
Test `apps/desktop/test/bill-number-clash.test.mjs` (24, mutation-checked).

### A496 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-15 (till 1.0.16) · Tills behind a branch server sometimes never got their update; branch-server access hardening
Owner, 2026-10-15: "check update function on server till setup sometimes the tills never gets updates". Five causes:
(1) a server holding its own downloaded update returned early from every check — a server is never closed, so it never
fetched the next version for its tills; (2) at launch the first check ran before the listener bound, so the server took
itself for a till; (3) under Electron a stalled download (or a hung latest.yml check) never times out and blocked every
later check; (4) a till waited on the server's copy with no end and no reason when the server could not fetch it;
(5) a copy left from before a roll-back was offered as newer.
**BUILT:** `autoUpdate.ts` `createUpdateLoop` always runs; "server" by role; a 15-minute no-progress watchdog cancels and
restarts; checks race 120 s; `updateShare.ts` tracks the server's fetch per version (`shareProgress`), offers only the
approved version (`offeredVersion`); a till downloads through the server's gateway live after 3 failed server fetches or
6 h (`tillShareVerdict`). Every decision logged in one sentence; Tech page › Updates shows the reason and the log; the
server's till-versions panel shows its fetch. Branch-server hardening (2026-10-15 audit): relayed changes never pushed by
the server, no device-key self-enrolment (`node_enrol_allowed` seeded once from known tills), proven device on roster /
report / since / cursors / reference / branding / tech-session, verify-pin limited per address, join refuses a keyed device,
gateway path decoded before its checks, branch staff of other branches dropped, roster version includes permissions,
TOFU pins marked unconfirmed, optional TLS-only. Tests `update-delivery` (37), `update-delivery-electron` (6),
`branch-server-hardening` (45).
**Owner decision pending:** a till set up by typing the server address and access code (not joined) after this build is
refused by the server on keyed routes.

### A490 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-15 (cloud + web + till 1.0.15; migration 134) · One permission catalogue: every report, view and action its own permission
Owner, 2026-10-14/15: "turn most of this features into permissions which can be set in one place … each report … a
permission … dont just focus on reports break even other views and how to limit what users see".
**FOUND (four code surveys):** 29 broad keys; `reports.view` opened every operational report, `reports.financial` every
financial one, `products.manage` the whole menu and its costs, `settings.manage` sixteen unrelated settings; `shifts.manage`
was checked in four places and existed nowhere (only the owner could pass); six catalogue keys were never enforced; many
routes had no check (reservations, parking, fuel, the staff list, turnover); the owner dashboard had no gates, the web POS
mixed keys with role-name lists, and the till had NINE different "is a manager" rules that disagreed (the owner was refused
the update restart; a staff.manage holder could create an owner on a till; the update bar's PIN check switched the
signed-in person; config:get handed the branch access code to any screen; shift:zreport bypassed blind close; a role
change reached the till only at the next sign-in). Cost prices and margins went to everyone who could read a product.
Owners' own database sessions could write admin-only columns directly (feature_flags, businesses — RLS FOR ALL).
**BUILT:** `shared/permissions.ts` — 63 fine keys in 11 groups (selling, drawers and the day, 14 reports one each, orders,
menu, stock, customers, expenses, staff, front of house, settings), each with the owner's words and Cashier / Manager
defaults; the 8 broad keys are LEGACY and expanded everywhere into exactly the fine keys they stood for (measured from the
code), so nobody gains or loses anything at the switch; older clients get a broad key only when every fine key behind it
is held. Cloud: one function for a person's keys (`lib/effectivePermissions`), tokens and requireAuth carry fine keys,
`requirePermission` refuses a non-catalogue key at load, every route converted (export routes need `reports.export` AND
the report's key), costs stripped server-side unless `menu.costs` / `reports.costs`, role-name checks gone except "the
owner's role is the owner" (`lib/ownerRole`), the role ceiling is by keys (`keysBeyond`), "back office" is a permission
rule (`isBackOffice`) for sign-in codes, device approval and routing; the till's own sign-in limited to what a till does
(`lib/tillScope`, dry-run until `TILL_SCOPE_ENFORCE`). Web: manager portal, its reports and the web POS gated per key
(discount, void and refund separately, Z-report blind without `reports.shifts` / `shifts.confirm`). Till: one rule
(`main/personAccess`, `renderer/lib/access`), every gate per key, the handlers that had none gated, the update bar asks a
PIN without signing anyone in (owner allowed), permissions refresh from the roster and the token renewal. Till changes
need fine keys, all of them, on the till and the cloud alike (`tillChanges.changeKeys` — expanding staff.manage would have
let any cashier change staff). Migration 134 registers the catalogue, rewrites every role's and person's grants, gives
what had no check to the roles that had it, and makes owners' database sessions read-only on feature_flags and businesses.

(92), `tests/till-change-keys.test.mjs` (6); `check-permission-catalogue` rebuilt (all apps, fine keys only) and in CI.

check stays open to everyone until it runs).

### A489 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-15 (till 1.0.15; no cloud change) · The shop network carried tokens, the access code and PIN hashes in plain HTTP
Owner, 2026-10-14 (branch server audit, item 2, "whats your call on number 2?"): mitigations in phase 1 (A485), then TLS in
its own release keeping the old http path during the move.
**FOUND:** every request between a till and its branch server was plain HTTP on the LAN — each till's cloud sign-in token
(through the A410 gateway, and update downloads), the branch access code (in every header, and handed out by the join),
the join grant's device key and one-time code, the staff roster with PIN hashes (`/node/roster`), and every sale. Anyone
on the shop's wifi could read them.
**BUILT:** `main/lanTls.ts`. The branch server makes its own certificate once (ECDSA P-256, self-signed, valid from 2020 for
20 years — a till with a wrong clock still connects) with no new dependency, and serves TLS and plain HTTP on the SAME port
(the first byte of each connection decides) — firewall rules, the beacon and saved addresses unchanged; `GET /node/tls`
hands out the certificate. A till PINS it (the exact certificate, no CA, no host name): a new till reads it first and joins
over TLS, both screens showing the same security code to compare; a till already joined pins it by itself within a minute
of its server answering TLS (after an encrypted health check with its access code); a repoint pins what its probe proved.
`node_url` stays `http://ip:port`; `lanFetch` sends it over TLS once pinned, every till call to the server goes through it
(nodeClient, the cloud gateway, the roster ping, update checks), and update downloads trust the pin through the
'electron-updater' session's certificate check. Once pinned a till never falls back to plain: another certificate is
"the branch server's identity changed" on the Tech page (Shop network row) with "Trust it again" (a technician or
`settings.manage`). Plain HTTP stays open for tills on older builds, each logged on the server every 30 minutes. Answers
are read whole before they are handed over (a status-only caller never holds a connection). Test
`apps/desktop/test/lan-tls.test.mjs` (52, real server and TLS; 6 mutations bite).
**NEXT:** once every till runs 1.0.15, a setting on the server to refuse plain HTTP.

### A488 · P3 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-14 (cloud + admin; no till change) · Clear test data said a trading day was open and never said which
Owner, 2026-10-14: "there is no open day i have closed all das".
**CAUSE:** `purge_test_data` (migration 123) counts the CLOUD's business days opened in the window with no `closed_at` or

after the window's end") with what to do: sync that till, update it if it is on an old build, preview again. Same rule as
the function. `routes/admin.ts`, admin `TestDataCard.tsx`; test `tests/test-data-clear.test.mjs`.

### A487 · P3 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-14 (cloud; no till change) · Clear test data said a till had not synced while Fleet said "just now"
Owner, 2026-10-14 (screenshots: Fleet "T1 · just now · 21:37"; Clear test data "Not synced since testing stopped: T1
(14 Oct 2026, 21:37)"): "why this conflict".
**CAUSE:** the window ends at "now" by default, and the preview named every till whose last sync was before the window's
end — a till that synced a minute earlier was always "behind". It also compared the times as strings.
**BUILT:** a till counts as behind only when its last sync is before the earlier of the window's end and 10 minutes ago
(`TILL_SYNC_GRACE_MS`), compared as times. A window that ended days ago behaves as before. `routes/admin.ts`; test
`tests/test-data-clear.test.mjs` (the owner's case, plus old windows and a till that never synced).

### A486 · P0 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-14 (cloud + till 1.0.14) · Security audit: writes that checked sign-in but not the business or the permission
Owner, 2026-10-14: "do it thoroughly do not assume read everybit or line of code".
**FOUND (read, not assumed):** `PUT /api/branches/:id/stock/:productId` checked only that the caller was signed in — no

staff-edit rule; on the till, `config:save` let any renderer call rewrite the till's identity, and branch prices and

**BUILT:** `branchForWrite` (business + `settings.manage` / `inventory.adjust`); `products.manage` on discounts /

### A485 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-14 (till 1.0.14) · Branch server audit: a till's rows could be skipped, re-sent to the wrong server, or relayed unchecked
**FOUND:** `nodeIngest` stopped at the first bad row (`break`) while the till marked every row not named as delivered — the
rest of the batch was lost; moving a till to another branch server never re-offered what the new one lacked; a till that
left stayed on the close-day list for ever; a close-day instruction had no date guard or expiry, and acks matched by
position; tills behind a server shared one key; refunds were not replicated to peers; a till's numbering was not
backfilled on the node; one bad event failed a whole pull; large batches had no size bound; verify-pin had no rate limit.
**BUILT:** `continue` past a bad row with `applied_ids` and `settleNodeBatch` / `advancePastFailures`; a node change
re-arms the outbox (`noteNodeTarget`, `rearmNodeOutbox`, `skipHeldByNode` via `/node/cursors`, a one-time 14-day re-offer);
transport errors are not counted as failures; "Forget this till" on Branch close plus a 7-day age-out; close-day checks its
date, instructions expire after 24 h, acks carry `node_instructions.uid`; per-device keys (`node_device_keys`,
`X-Device-Token`, stripped by the gateway); relayed staff changes take the role from `roles_cache`; refunds replicate
(`order_refunded`); `numberOwnRows` + backfill; `replicateToNode` on a 15 s tick; per-event try/catch; 2 MB batches halving
on 413; a tz-offset drift warning; verify-pin rate-limited with async bcrypt; pruning; network note on Tech and Install.
Report scope label says when other tills' copies are included. Test `apps/desktop/test/branch-server-audit.test.mjs` (92).
**NEXT:** TLS between the branch server and its tills — its own release, the http path kept during the move.

### A484 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-14 (till 1.0.14, local schema 72) · Till sync audit: a close during a push marked synced, sales stuck behind a missing drawer, refusals parked that a retry fixes
**FOUND:** shifts / floats / expenses were marked synced by id alone, so a close written while a push was in flight was
marked synced and never sent; reversals were sent after the reconcile; a 404 on a close was taken as done; 50 old sales
waiting on a drawer (424) blocked every newer sale; the staff token renewed without the A477 gate; `/init` renewed on any
error; a merged change was re-sent with its old id; a transient conflict was parked for good; the business date used the
machine clock; a stuck sync flag was never released; a pay-out lost the sale it was for (`order_id`); the queue was never
pruned; one push could carry every row.
**BUILT:** conditional marks (status / closed_at compared); reversals before reconcile (`reversalWaits`); close: 2xx or 409
`ALREADY_CLOSED` = done, 404 re-arms the drawer, 5xx waits, and the close sends `closed_at` / `closed_by`; 424 stamps
`drawer_wait_at` and the order page skips drawers that answered 424; staff renewal behind the gate with `X-Device-Id` and a
60 s throttle; renew only on a 401 from `/init`; requeued merges get a new change id; `sync_error` + transient conflicts
re-queued (`isDataErrorCode`); `businessDateNow`; `takeSyncFlag` / `releaseSyncFlag` (10-min stale); `pruneSyncedQueue` and
`sync_queue_status_idx`; 200 rows per table per push; julianday comparisons. The cloud keeps a pay-out's `order_id` when
that sale is already there, and leaves it empty (never refuses) when it is not. `REQUIRED_DESKTOP_SCHEMA` 72 (warn only;
`HARD_MIN` unchanged at 41). Test `apps/desktop/test/till-sync-audit.test.mjs` (61), `tests/sync-push-retry.test.mjs`.

### A477 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-14 (cloud + migration 131 + till 1.0.12) · One lost or stale renewal could lock a till out of the cloud for good
Owner, 2026-10-14: "how can we prevent such the way there is syn - synack - ack, this token refresh keeps messing us up,
imagine a high traffic client"; "the key should come with [the MAC and serial] just to confirm that this till is in the
system"; "I don't want a lot of warnings to the user and can we make logs bigger so that nothing can be skipped".
**Cause:** the owner's till renewed on 2026-10-12 ~09:20 EAT for the last time; afterwards every renewal answered
`TOKEN_REPLAYED` (a key two generations old — the till went back to older data, or the session was ended) and the cloud
revoked the whole session; the till had no device secret (`DEVICE_NO_SECRET`), so it needed a technician; its callers
retried many times a minute (429) for two days, and the 2 × 1 MB logs lost the start.
**BUILT:** renewal as a handshake (`lib/refreshHandshake.ts`, pure decision table): the new key is unconfirmed and the old
one stays valid until the till has written the new one to disk and confirmed it (`POST /api/auth/refresh/ack`, or the new
key's first use); asking again before confirming gets a fresh key; for a till an older key is refused alone
(`TOKEN_STALE`, session kept, owner alerted) — a person's session keeps the revoke-all rule. Machine identity
(`lib/tillIdentity.ts`): the till sends its MAC and SHA-256 of its Windows MachineGuid and BIOS serial; first sight is
stored (`user_devices`); a guid OR serial match passes, a MAC-only change passes and updates, a full mismatch is refused
(`DEVICE_MISMATCH`, session kept, owner alerted "used on another computer"); rejoin resets it; old tills without the
headers pass. A device secret on any renewal when the till has none, or (identity matched) when it lost its copy; Fleet
and admin show "no device secret". Till: disk is the only source of the key; write before ack; one 15-min gate for every
caller after a definite refusal, Retry-After honoured on 429; no cashier warnings (the owner email). Logs: 10 × 5 MB, a
repeat collapsed into "repeated N times between …", and `auth.log` (20 × 2 MB) of every renewal / ack / grant / sign-in.
Peers through a branch server forward the ack and the identity. Migration 131: `refresh_tokens.acked_at` (backfilled,
except a successor the old rotation left live — its first use confirms it), `user_devices` identity and alert columns.
Tests `tests/refresh-handshake.test.mjs` (40), `apps/desktop/test/refresh-handshake-till.test.mjs` (41),
`scripts/test-migration-131.mjs` (5); pins moved in till-sessions, syncEngine-failures, catalogue-refresh-signal, logFile.
**Order:** apply migration 131 with (or before) the cloud deploy; then tag 1.0.12. Limits: a modified client can omit the
headers; a motherboard swap with a Windows reinstall needs a rejoin.

### A473 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-14 (till 1.0.12) · The PIN pad took 8–12 s to sign in when the till's own session was refused or the line was slow

technician must rejoin it; its shift pushes were refused since 2026-10-12) and every PIN sign-in still asked the cloud,

checks the PIN on the till at once (the same answer A407 gave after the wait). A PIN the till knows (its staff list or a
saved sign-in) waits 4 s for the cloud, an unknown one 8 s; the whole exchange is bounded (5 s / 10 s). A cloud "no" is
still final. Test `apps/desktop/test/fast-unlock.test.mjs` (7); `tests/till-name.test.mjs` pin moved. **Owner action:**
the till on the owner's PC needs a technician rejoin (Tech page) — its sales and shifts have not reached the cloud.

### A465 · P2 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-13 (till 1.0.12) · A manager could put cash in / out or an expense only on the drawer of the till in front of them
Owner, 2026-10-13: "can they select on the current running shift where cash in, cash out or expense is being charged?" →
"It can be done on the desktop server only not a till"; and "remove the icons on the cards on the desktop overview but
leave the colors".
**Cause:** `shift:float` and `expense:create` always used the till's own open shift; a manager at the branch server could
not reach a cashier's drawer on another till.
**BUILT:** on the **branch server** (device_role node / office) with a manager signed in: Close Branch › **Drawers open now**
lists every open shift of the branch (cashier, till name, opened, cash expected) with **Cash in / out** and **Expense**;
Manager › Expenses gets **Which drawer**. The server never writes another till's row: `branchClose:shiftMoney` checks the
role, the manager, the amount, and that the till was heard from in the last minute and reports the shift open, then queues a
`shift_money` instruction on the A452 channel (`node_instructions`); the till's 15 s peer loop runs `executeShiftMoney` —
idempotent on the row id, refused if the shift is no longer open on that till ("record it on the shift now open"; never moved
to another shift) — into its own books (`addFloatToShift` / `recordExpense`, own device_id), pushes, and reloads its shift
screen (`shift:changedElsewhere`). So the cashier's Z-report, the cloud's expected cash and Close Branch agree, offline too.
The screen shows each one waiting / recorded / refused with the till's reason; Cancel only before the till picks it up. The
server's own drawer is recorded at once. Plain tills unchanged; a till on an older build is told to update. Also: the desktop
Overview cards have no icons (colours kept). Test `apps/desktop/test/server-drawer-money.test.mjs` (33);
`apps/desktop/test/overview-look.test.mjs` pin updated.

never deleted); `localChanges.ts` applies a rename / role (name + permissions from the saved roles) / (de)activation here
at once — an inactive person stays listed but does not sign in (`branchStaff.ts` filters status, the branch server does not
serve them) and their saved sign-in is dropped; `manage:updateStaff` goes till-first for name / role / status (`is_active`
mapped to status), else the cloud; cloud `changeApply.ts` judges a staff update like any update with the web's rules

### A452 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-12 (cloud + web + till 1.0.9) · Close Branch refused yesterday's open day and could not confirm the shifts that held it; no expected figures at confirm; expenses not filterable
Owner, 2026-10-12 (screenshot, two tills "refused": "This till's open trading day is 2026-10-11, not 2026-10-12. Check

**BUILT:** each till reports its shifts with its state every 15 s (`branchClose.ts` `ownShifts`: who, when, orders, sales,

### A451 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-12 (cloud + web; no till change) · The owner's void and refund failed with a 500; the report's overview did not add up to what was paid
Owner, 2026-10-12: "void is not working … it is an offline sale, I need to void and refund" — the browser console: `POST
/api/orders/8a523b99…/void 500`, twice (the second was not "already voided", so the first write itself failed). And the
Reports overview (screenshot): Gross Sales 8,900, M-Pesa 7,000 + Cash 2,050 = 9,050 (78.7% + 23.0%) against the till's
count 9,050 — "the total is off … we need a card of total sales inclusive VAT".
**Causes:** (1) an owner whose account has no `public.users` row signs in with the auth.users id (auth.ts, the logged
"fallback of last resort"); the void wrote it into `orders.voided_by` / `authorized_by` (and a refund into `refunded_by`),
which reference `users(id)` — refused every time. (Also found: `verifyPin` threw on a stored PIN hash of another shape —
`timingSafeEqual` of buffers of different lengths — failing every manager-PIN approval of the business with a 500.)
(2) each payment covers the bill + delivery fee + tip, while the sales count the bill; the methods' shares were of the sales.
**BUILT:** (1) `routes/orders.ts` `recordedPerson` — void and refund record a users row of the business (the owner's row
by `businesses.owner_id` when the sign-in carries none; else nobody), never an id the database refuses; `verifyPin` treats
an odd hash as no match. (2) `GET /api/reports/master` adds `totalDeliveryFees`, `totalTips`, `totalCollected`; the web
overview's first card is **Total Collected (incl. VAT)** with "sales + delivery + tips" under it, Gross Sales says
"(incl. VAT)", and the payment methods show a Total paid row, their shares of it (100%). Tests
`tests/void-owner-row.test.mjs` (5), `tests/report-collected.test.mjs` (5), `tests/owner-void-refund.test.mjs` (pins
updated); mutations confirmed. **Still to do (owner / support):** give the owner a `users` row (the sign-in log says
"no public.users row for this owner") — other owner writes that name the person may still be refused until then.
**BUILT 2026-10-13 (owner: "A451 is important and needed"):** the owner always signs in as a users row —
`routes/auth.ts` `ensureOwnerUserRow`: by email, else the row `businesses.owner_id` names, else one is created as for a new
client (the business's owner — else admin — role, active, the main branch), logged once. Used at sign-in, and at a
session's renewal (an owner session issued before is moved to the row — no sign-out needed). Test
`tests/owner-users-row.test.mjs` (6); mutations confirmed. The support step above is no longer needed.

### A450 · P2 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-12 (cloud + web + till 1.0.8) · A business renamed on the web kept its old name on the tills; the receipt's Buy Goods / Paybill line had no setting; no Approvals badge
Owner, 2026-10-12: "ensure the till always gets the correct business name — I changed a business name on the web but the
