### A449 · P2 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-12 (till 1.0.8) · A sync answer that stalled mid-body hung the till's sync; a wrong branch access code was silent
Found in the A446 session audit and noted there as open. (1) `syncFetch`'s time limit ended when the headers arrived: an
answer that stalled mid-body (a big menu on a weak line) held that pull — and every sync queued behind it — for good.
(2) A till given the wrong branch access code was refused by its branch server on every request; the log said so, nobody
else did — its sales stayed on the till, unseen by the cloud and the other tills, until someone opened the log.
**BUILT:** (1) the body is read inside `syncFetch` under its own time limit and handed back whole (`main/syncEngine.ts`).
(2) the branch server's own refusal (401/403 — not the cloud's) is remembered (`cloudGateway.ts` `nodeRefusal`, also from the
server health check in `nodeClient.ts`), cleared by the next request it accepts, reported in `sync:status` (`nodeRefused`)
and shown FIRST in the manager's sync notice: "The branch server refused this till's access code — sales are kept on this
till but reach nothing else. A technician re-enters the code (Install › Branch access code)". Tests: `test/sync-timeout.test.mjs`
(+2), `test/branch-gateway.test.mjs` (+2), `test/sync-notice.test.mjs` (+1); mutations confirmed.

### A448 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-12 (cloud + migration 129 + till 1.0.8, local schema 71) · An offline till could not add a printer — the till leaned on the cloud for every manager change
Owner, 2026-10-11/12: "a totally offline till can't add another printer — that's bad; they should be able to work
independently; cloud should never block a till from working … cloud and local instance complement one another but none is
superior unless an override is done — break this over-reliance on the cloud". On a clash: "if they are the same keep them,
if not notify the owner requesting approval"; "offline supersedes online when it comes to PIN change"; printers and the menu
both ("do both … I need them to complement, not fight one another").
**Cause:** every manager write on the till (a print station, a category, a product, a cashier, a PIN) went to the cloud first
and failed offline ("No connection — menu and staff changes need internet"); the till held only what the cloud sent it.
**BUILT:** rules in `shared/tillChanges.ts` (the same file on the till, the branch server and the cloud): what may change per
kind, how values compare (the till's 1 is the cloud's true; a new thing's name in any case), and the verdict. **Till:**
`main/localChanges.ts` + `main/changeQueue.ts` — the change is applied on the till at once (it prints, sells, signs in) and
kept in `local_changes` with the value seen before it (`base`); a refresh from the cloud does not undo a change still
waiting (`overlayLocalChanges` after every pull, stations refresh and staff list); sent on the 20-s beat and at once
(a change made mid-send goes in the next pass); behind a branch server it is handed to the server too (`POST /node/changes`,
applied there, its other tills see the server's change counter move and pull). A PIN is kept wrapped, never in the clear.
Manager screens: stations, categories, products (simple ones — an image, variants, modifiers or fuel still go to the cloud),
a cashier (with a role this till has saved) and **Change PIN** work offline; each row says "not on the cloud yet" / "with the
owner" / "refused: …", and a notice on the manager screens lists what has not settled. **Cloud:** `POST /api/changes`
(`lib/changeApply.ts`; the till's own session may send — the maker's own permissions are checked): **applied** (nobody else
changed it), **identical** (the same thing already there — kept once; a new station / category / product made in two places
takes the cloud's id, its printer follows), **awaiting** (changed differently elsewhere — NOT applied; the owner is notified)
or **refused** (with the reason: not allowed, a barcode or PIN someone else has, an owner role from a till). A PIN set on a
till wins over the cloud's unless another person has it. **Web:** Approvals (`/dashboard/approvals`) — the till's value next
to the cloud's; "Take the till's" / "Keep the cloud's" (owner or settings.manage; never a till's session). Migration 129
`change_requests` (one row per change, by the till's own id — a replay is answered the same; the PIN never stored).
Tests: `apps/desktop/test/till-first.test.mjs` (26 — the real till offline with a stand-in cloud on the same rules: a
station that prints, the menu, a clash approved and kept, the same station made twice, a cashier and a PIN offline, the
branch server), `tests/till-changes-cloud.test.mjs` (20 — the built route); mutations confirmed in both.
**Deploy order:** migration 129 → cloud → till 1.0.8. **Owner check:** pull the network cable on a till → Manager › Printers
› add "Barista" → Test print prints; change a price → it sells at it; reconnect → both on the web within ~20 s. Change the
same price on the web and (offline) on the till → Approvals on the web shows both; take the till's.

### A447 · P2 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-11 (till 1.0.7) · A manager could not record an expense from the manager screens

### A446 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-11 (cloud + till 1.0.7) · A new cashier "not recognised" for ~20 minutes; the lock screen's way out was closing the app
Owner, 2026-10-11: "the till should save cashiers pin instant when created on the local server or the cloud server no delay
— right now its 20 min and i am still getting an error; each till should keep a local copy of all staff pin related to that
branch"; the lock screen (screenshot) "Cannot check that PIN right now. Use Lock till and sign in again" — with no Lock till
on it; "funny messages like this till is not bound to a branch"; a new print station: 'No station "…"' on Test print
(screenshot); "check other breaking points … especially session, that's a disaster … in rush hour".
**Causes (read from the code and the branch server's log):** a till behind a branch server asked the SERVER for every PIN and
took its "no" as final; the server's staff list was refreshed only after a menu pull, and the cloud refused it the list
altogether when the cloud had not bound the server to a branch ("this device is not bound to a branch" — silently ignored);
the lock screen said "cannot check" for every failure (a wrong or unknown PIN included) and offered no way out; a till that
only ever signed people in through its server never recorded its branch; the printer screen listed the cloud's stations while
printing read the till's own copy, and station changes were not on the 20-s change check.
**BUILT:** cloud `GET /api/pos/branch-staff` serves EVERY joined till of the branch (not retired), binds a device with no
branch to its session's branch, and sends a version ("unchanged" when the till holds it). Till `main/staffRoster.ts`: every
till keeps its branch's list (branchStaff.ts, PIN hashes wrapped) — every 10 s on a server, 20 s on a till, at start, at once
when staff are created or changed on it (and it tells its server to refresh: `POST /node/roster/refresh`); from the cloud,
else the server's copy; never wiped by an empty answer; saved sign-ins of people no longer on it (or whose PIN changed) are
dropped. PIN check: the server's or the till's own "no" falls through to the cloud — only the cloud's "no" (or offline, every
local copy's) refuses; 8-s limit; a 429 "too many tries" uses the till's own list. A sign-in through the server records the
till's branch; a till that never did repairs at start (`tillBranchId`). Lock screen: `auth:unlock` checks the signed-in
person's PIN (this till's list, saved sign-ins, the server, the cloud) and changes nothing else — a colleague's correct PIN no
longer silently becomes the signed-in person, and an unlock no longer swaps a cloud session for an offline one; it says the
real reason and has "Sign out — another person signs in". Print stations: the station list fetched is also the till's copy;
`print_stations` is on the 20-s check, and a change the cloud reports is pulled from the cloud (not the server's possibly
older copy). **Session audit (read-only agent, every finding checked):** a sale is no longer counted towards 'failed' for a
connection problem (no internet, server off or without internet, timeout, 5xx, 429, 401) — an outage left one more sale
'failed' every 2.5 min and nothing retried them; sales left 'failed' that way go again once a push succeeds; time limits on
the till's cloud calls, the refresh through the server and the server's own refresh, the manager screens' calls; a staff
renewal that finishes after a cashier change is discarded; a queued sale of a cashier no longer signed in goes up under the
till's own session (it names its cashier) instead of being credited to whoever is signed in; the offline-session upgrade keeps
the PIN on a 401 / 429 ("later", not "never"). **Noted, not changed:** a wrong branch access code stops a till's cloud sync
silently (cloudGateway NodeRefusedError) — needs a banner; a reply body has no time limit after the headers (syncFetch).
Tests: `apps/desktop/test/staff-sync.test.mjs` (30 — a branch simulated: the real till behind a stand-in server and cloud;
8 mutations bite), `apps/desktop/test/station-copy.test.mjs` (6), `tests/staff-roster-cloud.test.mjs` (7), and
`sync-timeout.test.mjs` updated (a timeout is tried and stays pending). **Owner check:** create a cashier on the web — sign in
on a till within seconds; switch the server's internet off — the cashier still signs in; lock a till, enter a colleague's
PIN — "That is not X's PIN", nothing else changes; Sign out works; add a station on the web — Test print works on the till.

### A443 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-11 (till 1.0.6) · Tills behind a branch server never finished downloading an update
Owner, 2026-10-11: "i have done an approval but tills are not updating yet" — then "can we do it this way a server pulls the
update and shares it with the tills?" and "make the server update tills … if the till is off and comes online it can request
from the server or the server asks which version its running". Cause: since A410 a till's download went live through the
server's gateway, which cut every request at 60 s in total (`AbortSignal.timeout` covers the body) — the 205 MB installer
never finished on a shop line and started from nothing every hour.
**BUILT:** `main/updateShare.ts` — the server fetches the approved version once into its own folder, resuming a broken
download (Range), checks it against latest.yml's sha512 and size, and answers its tills' update requests from that copy over
the LAN (not ready → 503, never the live pass-through); the server updates itself from the same copy. Every till asks the
server every 2 minutes and at start ("I run X") — told of a newer version it checks with the cloud at once and downloads
from the server; it downloads only once the server holds the approved version (an older server: as before). The server lists
its tills and their versions (Tech page, `TillVersionsPanel`). The gateway's limit is now 60 s to start answering, then cut
only when nothing arrives for 60 s. Test `apps/desktop/test/update-share.test.mjs` (33; the real server on real ports; 7
mutations bite). **Owner check:** approve 1.0.6; update the server first (it downloads directly); install it (tray › Quit, or
Install now); within minutes the Tech page lists the tills and the version they run, and each till downloads from the server.

### A437 · P3 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-10 (till, next build) · Windows shutdown or log-off with a branch server running — not tested
Found 2026-10-10 checking the owner's question 2. In server mode closing the window only hides it
(`serverMode.keepServerWindowAlive`); Electron does not raise `before-quit` on a Windows shutdown or log-off, so the
close may be cancelled and Windows may wait on ZapTill ("this app is preventing shutdown"). Check on a real server PC:
Start › Shut down with the server running — it must close cleanly (the database closed, not cut). Fix if not: listen for
the window's `session-end` / `query-session-end` and quit properly. **Owner, 2026-10-10:** "proceed with your
recommendation" — build the clean close on shutdown / log-off.
**BUILT:** `serverMode.ts` `closeCleanlyOnSessionEnd` on every till's window: `query-session-end` lets the window close
(never vetoes the shutdown); `session-end` closes the database at once (`closeLocalDb`) and exits — Windows ends the
process right after, so nothing asynchronous is relied on. The LAN server is not stopped through `stopNodeServer` (that
announces "no longer serving", which would take ZapTill out of start-with-Windows), and `leaveServerMode` no longer clears
the login item on the way out (tray Quit, shutdown). Test `apps/desktop/test/server-notice.test.mjs` (with A436). **Owner
check:** on the server PC with ZapTill running, Start › Shut down — Windows does not wait on ZapTill; after power-on and
sign-in ZapTill starts, the tills reconnect, no sale is missing.

### A435 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-10 (till, next build; option a) · The branch server is not a Windows service — after a power cut it is down until someone logs into Windows
Owner, 2026-10-10 (asking): "server autostarts and never closes even when the application is closed so that it can keep
syncing throughout". **Checked (code):** closing the window hides it to the tray and every sync loop and the LAN server
keep running (A427: `serverMode.ts`, `index.ts` window-all-closed) — so that part holds. But it starts as a Windows LOGIN
item for the one Windows user (`setLoginItemSettings`), not a service: after a power cut or a Windows Update restart the
branch has no server until that user logs in (or the PC auto-logs in); a different Windows user does not start it; a crash
or Task Manager kill is not restarted; "Quit" in the tray quits; `prevent-app-suspension` stops idle sleep only, not a
closed lid or a manual sleep; updates install only on a restart. **Options (owner to choose):** (a) set the server PC to log
in automatically + a scheduled task that restarts ZapTill if it is not running (small); (b) run the branch server part as
a real Windows service that starts before login (large — the sync and LAN server split from the window). Recommended: (a)
now, (b) with the Android/tablet work. **Decided (owner, 2026-10-10):** "let's work with your recommendation" — (a) now.
**BUILT (a):** `main/serverWatchdog.ts` — entering server mode also creates a Windows scheduled task ("ZapTill branch
server"; the dev build its own) that starts ZapTill with `--watchdog` every 5 minutes, as the signed-in user. Running → the
launch meets the single-instance lock and ends, the window untouched (`second-instance` ignores `--watchdog`); not running
(a crash, a Task Manager kill) → it starts, so the branch has its server back within 5 minutes. A Quit from the tray writes
a flag and a watchdog launch then stays down until ZapTill is opened by hand (a deliberate quit stays quit); Restart is not
a quit. Leaving server mode removes the task. The technician's steps (`components/ServerKeepRunning.tsx`, on setup when
Branch server or Office is chosen, and in the technician console on a server): set the PC to sign in to Windows by itself
(netplwiz), never sleep when plugged in, leave ZapTill open. Still a login item, so it needs Windows signed in — (b), a real
service, remains for later. Test `apps/desktop/test/server-watchdog.test.mjs` (10; 4 mutations bite), in CI. **Owner
check:** on the server PC, end ZapTill in Task Manager — within 5 minutes it is running again; Quit from the tray — it
stays closed; open it — it serves again. Restart the PC (auto sign-in set) — ZapTill starts without anyone.

Owner, 2026-10-10, after A431/A432: "yes if they have logged in as the manager, and under sales report it should cover all
tills when logged in as the manager". **Before:** a shift could be confirmed only on the till that held it (or the web);
Sales › Orders opened on "This till", Item Mix and Shift report were this till's only. And a shift confirmed on the web
was never confirmed on the till that held it — that till's Close Day kept waiting for it (A365 left this gap).
**BUILT (cloud, `routes/shifts.ts`):**
- `POST /api/shifts/:id/manager-confirm` — the confirm route's own rules (`confirmShiftRoute`), as the signed-in manager or
  a manager's PIN, never the replay field `confirmed_by` (the holding till's alone). Its own path, listed in
  `lib/terminalWrites.ts` MANAGER_WRITES: a person's sign-in only, never the till's device token.
- `GET /api/shifts/:id/zreport` — any shift at the branch as a Z-report in the till's own shape (`lib/shiftZReport.ts`):
  sales refund-adjusted, the drawer as it counts (refund rows in), floats, expenses (cash out of the drawer, others off
  their method), voids, the confirmation (awaiting: what to recount; confirmed: by whom). A manager only, own branch.
- `GET /api/shifts/state` also answers the confirmation (when, who, the counts, the reasons).
- `/branch-report` adds Item Mix for every till (`topProducts`, order lines paged) and each shift's methods to recount.
**BUILT (till):**
- Confirm on a shift awaiting a manager — on the Overview's shift report and Sales › Shift report — for a signed-in
  manager (`shift:canConfirm`). This till's shift: its own record, as Close does. Another till's: the cloud
  (`shift:remoteConfirm`, `ConfirmShiftModal remote`), the same blind recount.
- `syncEngine.pullShiftConfirmations` (every 20 s): this till's closed shifts awaiting a manager, already on the cloud,
  take a confirmation made elsewhere as it stands (`confirm_sync = 'synced'`, no push back) — Close Day stops waiting.
- Sales › Shift report lists every till's shifts (the cloud, `manager:branchShifts`) with the till's name; this till's
  open from its own records (offline too), another till's from `manager:remoteZReport`; offline it says it shows this
  till's only. Orders opens on "All tills" (offline → this till, said so). Item Mix and the Overview's Top sellers read the
  branch (`manager:branchDay`), and say when they are this till only.
Tests `tests/shift-zreport.test.mjs` (14; 6 mutations bite) and `apps/desktop/test/branch-shifts-confirm.test.mjs` (12; 4
bite), in CI; `shift-reports` and `branch-day` pins moved with the screen. `terminal-write-guard` unchanged and passing.
**Owner check:** close a shift on till A; on till B sign in as a manager — Overview › Shift report shows it "Awaiting
manager" with Confirm; confirm it — within ~20 s till A's Close Day no longer waits for it. Sales › Shift report on B
opens A's Z-report; Item Mix shows both tills' items.

### A431 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-10 (cloud + till, next build) · A manager on one till cannot see the other tills' sales or shifts
Owner, 2026-10-09: "the manager should view sales across all tills no matter the till they have logged into, the server
they should also see the same — right now it's not that way, shifts are not syncing across for the manager to view".
**Cause (read):**
- **Sales.** The Overview reads the till's own database (`main/managerReports.ts` `getSalesSummary`, no till filter). The
  cloud never sends a till the other tills' sales, so without a branch server a till's Overview is its own sales only.
  With a branch server the rows do arrive (`/node/sync`, `/node/since`, every 30 s) — only when every till has joined it.
  The one branch-wide view is Sales › Orders › "All tills at this branch" (the cloud, `manager:branchOrders`).
- **Shifts.** Every shift query on the till is limited to THIS till (`COALESCE(device_id,'') = <this till>`): the shift
  report list (`shiftService.ts` `listShifts` — "a peer's shifts are that till's to report"), the open drawer
  (`getOpenShift`), the shifts waiting for a manager (`awaitingConfirmation`), the day's summary, the expenses. So another
  till's shifts never show — not even on the branch server, which holds them. The confirmation columns are not passed
  between tills at all.
- The cloud has them all (`GET /api/shifts`, used by the web's Shift reports page), but the till never asks it for them;
  the cloud's reports (`/api/reports/*`) refuse a till (`requireWebSurface`).
**Fix:** a manager's Overview reads the branch from the cloud — through the branch server on a till behind one (A410) —
and says what it shows; when the cloud cannot be reached it falls back to what the till holds and says so. The shift
report (A432) lists every till's shifts the same way. Acting on a shift (confirming, closing the day) stays as it is.
**BUILT (cloud):** `GET /api/shifts/branch-report?from&to&tz_offset_min` (`routes/shifts.ts`; shaped by
`lib/branchReport.ts`): the branch's completed orders in the range — refund-adjusted by `orderTax`, paged past the row cap
— as the till's Overview draws them (revenue, orders, average, VAT, CTL, refunds, discounts, tips, the method split, the
hours in the branch's own time) plus each till's share (by its code, else its label; the web POS as "Web Till"), and every
shift open in the range (A432). A manager only (`callerMayConfirm` — never a cashier, whose close is blind, nor the till's
own session, A415); the caller's branch (`branchScope`); at most a month. Open to the till, unlike `/api/reports`.
**BUILT (till):** `main/branchDay.ts` — `manager:branchDay` asks the cloud with the MANAGER's sign-in (`cloudFetch`, so
through the branch server on a peer, A410); no manager sign-in, no connection or an older cloud → what this till holds,
with no till filter (`// branch-wide`: every till on a branch server), and the reason. All three Overviews (restaurant,
petrol, retail) read it instead of `salesSummary`, and a line at the top says what they show: "All tills at this branch ·
from the cloud", or amber with the reason. "By till" when more than one till sold. Top sellers still reads the till and
says "(this till)" unless it is a branch server. Unchanged: Sales › Current shift / Shift report / Expenses and Close Day
stay this till's (acting on a drawer is still the till's own); Orders keeps its "All tills" switch.
Tests `tests/branch-report.test.mjs` (14; 5 mutations bite) and `apps/desktop/test/branch-day.test.mjs` (10; 4 bite), in
CI. **Owner check:** two tills, a sale on each; sign in as a manager on either — the Overview's revenue is both, "By till"
lists both, the shift report shows both drawers. Pull the cable — it says it shows this till only, and why.

### A429 · P2 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-10 (till next build, schema 69 + web + cloud) · Payment methods are hard-coded — the manager picks a branch's methods from a list of Kenya's common ones
Owner, 2026-10-09: "The payment method now we have them hard coded, mpesa, card, cash glovo can we list common payment
method and they are selected by the managers branch and they appear on the till by default cash and mpesa are the only one
selected, find all common payment method and delivery services in kenya and hardcode them." **Today:** the built-ins are
fixed in code and cannot be switched off — the till `cash · mpesa · card · glovo` (`lib/payment.ts` `LegMethod`,
`components/PaymentModal.tsx` `METHOD_META`), the web POS `cash · mpesa · card · credit` and no Glovo
(`pages/pos/PaymentModal.tsx`, `SplitPaymentPanel.tsx` `ALL_METHODS`), with their own copies in History
(`POSOrderHistoryTab.tsx`), the shift count (`ShiftPanel.tsx`, `ShiftModal.tsx`), the Z report labels (`ZReportView.tsx`)
and the daily sales report (`main/dailySalesReport.ts` `MODE_ROWS`). A business can add its own methods
(`payment_methods`, migration 86 — business only, no branch); they come after the built-ins. The cloud already takes any
`^[a-z0-9_]{1,40}$` code (migration 89), so no database list to widen. Glovo is a payment method, not an order type
(the reason is in `payment.ts`); Uber Eats and Bolt Food are nowhere.
**The list to hard-code (researched 2026-10-09):**
- Money: **Cash** · **M-Pesa** (Till or Paybill) · **Airtel Money** · **T-Kash** (Telkom) · **Card** (Visa / Mastercard on
  the PDQ) · **Bank transfer / Pesalink** · **Cheque** · **On account (credit)** · **Voucher / gift card** · **Room charge**
  (hotels; exists).
- Delivery apps: **Glovo** (largest; Uber agreed to buy its parent in July 2026, the apps stay separate until the deal
  closes in 2027) · **Uber Eats** · **Bolt Food** · **Yum Deliveries** (small). Jumia Food left Kenya in December 2023.
**Needed:** one fixed catalogue in `shared/` (code, name, colour, kind — cash / mobile money / card / bank / account /
delivery app — and what it needs: a reference, the M-Pesa prompt). A per-branch setting (business default, branch
override, the A387 pattern) of which are switched on; the till and web POS show only those, then the business's own
methods. **New branch: Cash and M-Pesa only.** Every hard-coded list above reads the catalogue instead. Codes never change
— `cash` (the drawer count) and `mpesa` (the STK prompt and C2B matching, `routes/mpesa.ts`) stay as they are. Reports
and History still show a method that is switched off today if old sales used it. **Decided (owner, 2026-10-10):** "yes
they keep them but the manager can still turn it off"; then, the same day, replacing that: "add them but as toggles — by
default the current payment methods are on but the manager can turn them on or off; add the others but the manager has to
turn them on; per branch is also valid and I like it". So: every method is a switch per branch. **On until switched off:**
the methods the till and web POS have today — Cash, M-Pesa, Card, Glovo, On account. **Off until switched on:** Airtel
Money, T-Kash, Bank transfer / Pesalink, Cheque, Voucher / gift card, Room charge, Uber Eats, Bolt Food, Yum. The same for a
new branch and an existing one (no 90-day look-back).
**BUILT:** `shared/paymentCatalogue.ts` (copied to the till, the web and the cloud; check-shared-sync) — the 14 methods with
code, name, icon, kind, what reference to take, and on / off by default; On account is marked web-only (it needs a customer
with a credit account, which only the web POS has). Setting `payment_methods_enabled` — a JSON list of codes, business
default + branch override (the A387 pattern): the cloud refuses anything not in the catalogue (`routes/business.ts`,
`routes/branches.ts`) and sends `paymentMethodsEnabled` in /pos/init (the branch's own wins; absent = the defaults). The
till keeps it (`device_config.payment_methods_enabled`, schema 69; REQUIRED 69), pulls it and relays it to the branch's
other tills through the branch server (`referenceBundle.ts`). **The till's payment screen** (`components/PaymentModal.tsx`)
shows the branch's switched-on methods then the business's own (A96) — no fixed list any more; the first leg starts on cash
where the branch takes cash, else on its first method; each method's reference box says what to take ("Bolt order #").
**The web POS** (`pages/pos/PaymentModal.tsx`): cash / M-Pesa / card / On account where switched on, then the catalogue's
other switched-on methods and the business's own (settling at once, like a card); split payment offers only what the
branch takes (the catalogue's other methods are not in split payment yet — single payment only). **Switches:** the till's
Manager › Settings › "Payment methods — this branch" (Money / Delivery apps; saved on the cloud for the branch — needs a
connection; a manager's sign-in, settings.manage; `terminalWrites.ts` lets a till's manager reach the branch settings
path) and the web's Settings › Branches › a branch › Payment methods ("Back to the default"). Colours for the new methods
(`paymentColours.ts`; T-Kash's blue recorded in A329's classification); the Z-report and the daily sales report name every
method ("AIRTEL MONEY", "Bolt Food"). Old sales by a method switched off still show everywhere (reports read the sales).
Codes unchanged: `cash` (the drawer), `mpesa` (STK and C2B). Seen rendered: the till's payment screen with Cash, M-Pesa,
Card, Airtel Money, Uber Eats and a business's own "Staff meal" (Glovo switched off); the till's switches, a tap saving the
branch's new list. The web's screens type-checked, not seen (they need a signed-in cloud session here). Test
`tests/payment-catalogue.test.mjs` (20; 5 mutations bite). **Owner check:** web › Settings › Branches › a branch ›
Payment methods: switch on Airtel Money, off Glovo; on a till of that branch (after a sync) the payment screen has Airtel
Money and no Glovo; the web POS the same; a sale by Airtel Money shows in History, the Z-report and the daily report.

### A421 · P2 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-09 (till, next build) · Closing a shift on the till leaves the cashier signed in, at "Opening float"
Owner, 2026-10-09: "When a shift is closed it should log the user out back to log in not opening float the next cashier might
be confused and open the next shift with the wrong cashier details". **Today, till:** `ShiftPanel.handleClose` → `onShiftChange(null)`
→ the day gate says `needsShift` → `POSPage` shows `OpenDrawerModal` ("Opening float", with only a small "Not you? Sign out")
under the person who just closed. The next cashier can open the next shift under that name. Also, not yet tested: the
"Opening float" modal and the "Shift closed" panel are both `fixed inset-0 z-50` and the modal comes later in the page, so
it may cover the closed panel and its "Manager: confirm now". **The web POS already does this right:** `CashierScreen.tsx`
`onShiftClosed` clears the cashier's session and goes back to the PIN screen. **Decided (owner, 2026-10-09):** "the moment they close a
shift it should log the cashier out not for the cashier to select sign out or get the opening float pop up". So the till
signs the cashier out to the PIN screen as soon as the close is saved — no Done to press, no "Sign out" to pick, and
"Opening float" is never shown to the person who closed. The next person to sign in is asked for the float. To settle in the
build: the closed panel's "Manager: confirm now" goes with it — a manager confirms from Manager › Shifts (A365) as they can
already. The owner's own description of today and what changes (2026-10-09): "cashier logs in, gets open drawer pop
up, they enter the amount they are opening with and they start to sell, once done they close their shift, enter amount
sold close, they get open your drawer, with a message not you sign out which they have to tap for the second cashier to
sign in … opening remains the same, closing is where i want a change: once they close their shift take them directly to
the keypad for the other cashier to log in, no open drawer". Opening is unchanged. **Owner check:** close a shift — the
PIN keypad at once, not "Opening float"; the next cashier signs in and is asked for their float.
**BUILT:** `pages/ShiftPanel.tsx` takes `onSignOut`: a cashier's close (blind — every cashier, 0.6.29) signs out the
moment the cloud/till answers, no panel; a manager's close (and a force close) still shows the closed panel to print the
Z-report or "Manager: confirm now", and "Done — sign out" or ✕ signs out. `POSPage` passes it (`onShiftClosed`) and no

### A417 · P2 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-10 (till, next build; parts 1 and 2) · No on-screen keyboard on a touch till; the device's keyboard can cover the field
Owner, 2026-10-09: "when a cashier taps on a text box can we find a way to make the keypad appear something like the image
attached without covering the text box where a value is being keyed in?" — the image (2026-10-09): the till's "Till locked" screen on a touch PC, with the
Windows touch keyboard up over the bottom half, hiding ZapTill's own PIN keypad. **Found from the image:** the lock screen
focuses a hidden PIN input so a physical keypad works (`components/LockCurtain.tsx` `lock-pin-input`, `type="password"`,
`inputMode="numeric"`); on a touch PC Windows takes that focus as "the user is typing" and opens its keyboard over the
screen's own keypad. Any screen with its own keypad must stop Windows doing that (`inputMode="none"` on the hidden input,
checked on a touch PC — the physical keypad must still work). **Today:**
the only on-screen keypads are the PIN pads (`PinPage.tsx`, `POSLoginScreen.tsx`); other fields set `inputMode="numeric"`
at most and rely on the device's own keyboard; nothing keeps a focused field in view. **Needed:** an on-screen keyboard
(numbers for amounts, letters for text) on the till and the web POS that opens when a field is tapped, sits where it does
not cover that field (the field scrolled into view above it), and closes on Done. Like the Windows one in the image (letters, numbers, backspace, enter), but ZapTill's own, so it never
covers the field. **Decided (owner, 2026-10-09):** on every till — no per-till setting. A physical keyboard keeps
working alongside it.
**Part 1 BUILT (the screenshot):** `components/LockCurtain.tsx` — the hidden PIN input is `inputMode="none"`, so Windows
keeps its keyboard shut over the lock screen's keypad; the physical keypad still types (the input is still focused). The
PIN screen reads keys from the window with no input, so it never had the problem. Test `test/lock-keypad-osk.test.mjs`
(3; the mutation bites), in CI. To check on the touch till: lock it — the Windows keyboard does not come up.
**Part 2 BUILT:** `components/OnScreenKeyboard.tsx`, mounted at the till's root (every screen), rules in `lib/osk.ts`. A
field TAPPED with a finger or pen opens it (a mouse click or a physical keyboard does not — every till, no setting, and a
till with a real keyboard is not bothered). Numbers (7-8-9 … 00, Clear, ⌫, Done) for an amount, quantity, phone or PIN;
letters like the owner's picture (a number row, q–p, a–l, z–m, ⇧, &123, space, Done, ✕) otherwise. It docks at the bottom
of the screen, or at the top when the field is low (`oskDock`) — the field being typed in is never under it, inside
pop-ups too. While it is up the field asks Windows for no keyboard (`inputmode="none"`), restored on close; keys type
through the field's own value setter and an `input` event (React's onChange sees typing) and never take focus; Done sends
Enter. Not served: the lock screen's hidden PIN (inputMode "none"), read-only/disabled fields, checkboxes, `data-osk="off"`.
Test `apps/desktop/test/osk.test.mjs` (16; 3 mutations bite), in CI. **Owner check (touch till):** tap the opening-float
box — the number pad comes up below it; tap a search box near the bottom — the keyboard goes on top; with a mouse, nothing.

### A427 · P2 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-09 (cloud + desktop 1.0.4) · Every till behind a branch server had to be set up by hand
- **Asked (owner, 2026-10-09):** "when installing the app should be scanning from a local server and pick configs from
  it, i should not be configuring each till after enrolling, it should only ask if i allow it to join the server or
  not" — then: "the server to broadcast in the network and the till or any installation to listen; if none exist the
  tech gets the screen to select; add the server as a service that never sleeps when the computer is on; when the app is
  closed it remains open in the task panel; the till codes and branch code remain, nothing changes there".
- **Built:**
  - *Beacon* (`serverBeacon.ts`): the branch server broadcasts on UDP 4199 every 3 s — its port and names only, nothing
    secret. Setup on a new machine listens 6 s first; servers heard are listed; none heard → the usual setup screens.
  - *Allow* (`serverJoin.ts`, `/node/join`, `/node/join/status` — the only two server routes open without the access
    code): the till asks; the server shows "<name> at <address> wants to join" over any screen (`JoinPrompt`), Allow /
    Deny. On Allow the server asks the cloud for ONE ordinary enrolment code for its branch (`POST /api/pos/join-code`:
    confirmed branch server only, its own licensed branch, 10 an hour) and keeps it, with the cloud address, business,
    branch and its access code, for that till — handed over once, to the holder of the request's private token. The
    till saves the server address and code, then enrols through the server (A410) with that code, getting its own
    session (A415). Setup ends on the usual last step with branch locked and the server filled in; the till code is
    typed as before.
  - *Always on* (`serverMode.ts`): while a machine serves its branch it starts with Windows, keeps the computer awake
    (prevent-app-suspension; the screen may still turn off), and closing its window hides it to the tray (Open /
    Restart — installs a downloaded update / Quit). A plain till is unchanged.
  - Installer: UDP 4199 inbound, private profile (as TCP 4100-4103).
- **Trade-off (owner's call):** a branch server can now add tills to its own licensed branch without an admin-issued
  code; every one is logged (`[tillJoin]`) and appears in the admin portal's device list. The hand-over travels over
  the shop LAN in plain HTTP, like all branch traffic.
- **Test:** `tests/till-join-code.test.mjs` (9; the real route, guard and redeem), `apps/desktop/test/server-join.test.mjs`
  (37; real UDP, the real branch server over HTTP). Mutations bite: no server-confirmation check (2), grant handed out
  twice (2).

### A426 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-09 (cloud) · Tills behind a branch server: "This branch server has no staff roster yet"
- **Reported (owner, 2026-10-09):** configuring tills with a local server, every till said "this branch server has no
  staff roster yet", while the same staff PINs signed in on the server itself.
- **Found:** two readings of one rule. PIN sign-in (`/auth/verify-pin`): a person with NO branch assigned works at
  every branch. The branch server's roster (`GET /api/pos/branch-staff`): only people with THIS branch explicitly
  assigned. In a shop where staff are not tied to a branch (the usual single-branch set-up) the roster was empty: the
  server stored nothing, served nothing, and its own PIN sign-in still worked because that goes to the cloud.
- **Fixed:** `apps/server/src/lib/branchAccess.ts` `worksAtBranch()` — the one rule, used by both routes. No till
  change; the server's next menu sync stores the full roster and the tills take it from the server.
- **Still true (by design):** only staff whose PIN is stored in the current (bcrypt) form are on the roster — anyone
  with an older PIN form drops in after one online sign-in.
- **Test:** `tests/branch-staff-roster.test.mjs` (11; the real `worksAtBranch` from the build + pins that both routes
  use it). Mutation bites: the old "only explicitly assigned" rule fails 3.

### A425 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-09 (desktop 1.0.4) · A re-uploaded menu left duplicate required choices on the till — the item could not be rung
- **Reported (owner, 2026-10-09):** "why does this menu keep duplicating its variants? when i upload it clients cant sell"
  — with the pizza menu workbook (one Size group per pizza: Medium 0, Large +200…+350).
- **Found:** the workbook is clean and the cloud is right — each upload keeps the product's one "Size" group, replaces
  its options with new rows and removes copies an earlier upload left (A389). The till's catalogue pull only ever
  INSERTed and UPDATEd variant and add-on rows (`ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE`), never removed one, and nothing else on the
  till clears them (`clearCatalogue` runs only on a first join; a rejoin keeps the catalogue, A415). So every upload added
  another Medium and Large to the till, and a "Size" group the cloud had removed stayed — each marked Required. The
  POS refused the item until every "Size" was picked ("Please select a Size"); a peer took the same rows from its branch
  server's snapshot. Deleting rows in the cloud database could not help the tills.
- **Fixed:** `apps/desktop/src/main/choicePrune.ts` — after the pull's upserts, in the same transaction, a product whose
  choices the till received has exactly the pulled groups and options (variants and add-ons alike); options of a group
  that is gone are removed. A product whose fetch failed keeps what it has (a network blink never strips a menu); a
  product with no variants upstream has none on the till; the branch server's snapshot covers every product, so peers
  heal on their next pull. Sales are untouched (a sale carries the chosen names). Logged when anything is dropped.
- **Recovery:** none needed — the first pull after 1.0.4 installs heals every till.
- **Test:** `apps/desktop/test/choice-prune.test.mjs` (14; the real compiled module on localDb.ts's own tables with the
  pull's own upsert SQL, through three uploads — reproduces the bug without pruning, then heals it). Mutations bite:
  dropping the per-option check, dropping the orphan sweep. CI step "Desktop menu choices follow the cloud".

### A415 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-06 (cloud + till 1.0.3; migration 127) · The till's session was the owner's; a lost one needed a reset
Owner, 2026-10-06 (Pollo's till on the PIN screen: "This branch server has no staff roster yet." and "Sign out / switch
account"): "remove any linkage with the desktop app using owners credetials, we find a way to use some key or something
that links the till to the business id and branch id never the owners session at all remove it totally even the
message at the bottom of the screen … add a way a technician can rejoin the app back to the bussiness rather than
reseting it". And: "too many log in attempts on the web yet it was only one attempt". **BUILT:**
- **The till signs in as itself** (`lib/deviceGrant.ts` buildDeviceTokenPayload): its token names the till (deviceId),
  the business and the branch — no person (userId null), isOwner false, branch-locked. `/enrol/redeem`, `/device-token`
  and `/refresh` all mint it. Every request checks the TILL (`middleware/auth.ts`: its user_devices row approved and not
  retired — retiring or revoking it cuts it off at once), never the owner's account. A pre-A415 till session (the
  owner's id on the till) is refused for requests (TOKEN_REPLACED) and replaced by the till's own on its next renewal —
  worked out before the old token is spent, so a till that may not renew keeps nothing half-done.
- **Nothing of the owner left:** admin enrolment codes name no owner (no `created_by`, no owner lookup); the till's
  device row and session rows name no person (migration 127: user_id / created_by nullable, and cleared on every
  existing till row, till session and code); `/desktop-login` removed outright; the till's session row holds its own
  device id. A step that needs a person never counts the till as one (`callerMayConfirm` false for a till): approving a
  void or refund, confirming a shift or a pay-out needs that person's PIN (the till's screens already ask for it). A
  sale is credited to the cashier the till names when the roster validates it — else nobody, never the owner
  (`lib/cashier.ts` mayClaim; the A169 caveat is closed).
- **On the till:** "Sign out / switch account" (PIN screen) and "Sign out business" (manager screen) are gone, and so
  is the auth:logout channel behind them. **Technician console › Rejoin this till** (business ID + a fresh code from
  the admin portal): joins the SAME till again (approved, un-retired, new device secret) and keeps everything on it —
  sales waiting to sync, shifts, menu, settings. Gated in main on an open technician session; audited; only the till's
  own business, and a code for another branch is refused before it is spent. A branch server with no staff roster yet
  checks PINs on the till's saved sign-ins instead of turning everyone away.
- **"Too many attempts" after one try:** every /api/auth call shared one counter per address (30 / 15 min, successes
  included), and a till retrying a refused renewal used it up for everyone at that address. Now only FAILED attempts
  count, and a till's renewals (/refresh, /device-token, /logout) have their own counter per till (`lib/authLimits.ts`).
Tests `tests/till-own-signin.test.mjs` (17, real routes + middleware; mutations bite), `apps/desktop/test/till-rejoin.test.mjs`
(11), `scripts/test-migration-127.mjs` (5, PGlite); 15 existing tests moved to the till's own token. **Deploy order:**
migration 127 BEFORE the cloud. **Owner check:** on Pollo's till, long-press the logo → technician console → Rejoin this
till with a fresh code for its branch — the PIN screen works, the sales waiting on it reach the cloud, and nothing on
the PIN screen offers to sign the till out.

### A414 · P2 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-06 (desktop 1.0.3; migration 126) · Wastage could only be recorded on the web
Owner, 2026-10-06: "Recording wastage on the till itself" — decided "save on till, sync later". **BUILT:** Manager ›
Stock › Wastage on the till (`components/TillWastage.tsx`) for anyone with inventory.waste / inventory.adjust (checked
on the till too). A recording is kept on the till at once (`main/tillWastage.ts`, maintenance_state `wastage_pending`)
and sent to POST /api/wastage now, or before each pull / every push pass / the 20 s beat — through the branch server on
a peer (A410). It carries its own id (`wastage_entries.client_id`): sent again after a lost answer, the cloud returns the
existing entry, never a second one. The person and the time are the till's (`recorded_by_name`, `recorded_at` — kept
by the cloud only from a till, and only a real time in the last 30 days). A refusal (more than the branch holds, an
item gone) ends the wait and shows on the screen with the reason until dismissed. Items: the cloud's list (with what
the branch holds), kept for offline; else the till's own products. The expired / expiring list (A413) shows at the top
with Write off. A159's till allowlist gains exactly `POST /api/wastage` — voiding (stock back) stays a person's.
Test `apps/desktop/test/till-wastage.test.mjs` (14, real SQLite + syncEngine; 4 mutations bite). **Owner check:** pull
the cable, record 2 × an item as Spoiled — it says "Saved on this till"; plug in — within ~20 s it is in the web's
Wastage log under the cashier's name and the time it was recorded, once.

### A413 · P2 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-06 (cloud + web + till 1.0.3; migration 126) · No batches or expiry dates for stock
Owner, 2026-10-06: "Batch and expiry-date tracking for stock" — decided: products AND ingredients; what is left in each
batch WORKED OUT oldest-expiry first from the stock level. **BUILT:** `stock_batches` (migration 126): one delivery of
one item at one branch — quantity received, expiry date, lot number (optional), source (restock / GRN / manual). It
holds no balance: `lib/batches.ts` lays the branch's current stock over the batches from the latest expiry back, so
whatever has gone (sales, recipes, wastage, counts) went from the earliest expiry first; stock beyond the batches is
"no batch recorded" (older, so it went first). Sales, tills and offline sync are untouched and the figures can never
disagree with the stock level. Recorded when stock is received — product restock (in pieces for a by-piece product),
ingredient add, every GRN line (both GRN screens) — when an expiry date or lot is given; never failing the receipt.
Stock › Expiry (owner) and Manager › Expiry (`components/Expiry.tsx`): expired and expiring-within-N-days first, with
value at cost; Write off → the wastage log as Expired with the batch named (`wastage_entries.batch_id`); Add a batch
for stock already on the shelf; fix a date; remove a batch entered by mistake (the owner). Routes `/api/batches`.
Tests `tests/batches.test.mjs` (15; 4 mutations), `scripts/test-migration-126.mjs` (5, PGlite, every migration).
Not done: a transfer between branches does not carry its batches (the receiving branch can add them); the clear-test-data
tool does not remove batches (they show nothing once their stock is gone). **Owner check:** restock 24 × an item with an
expiry 5 days out — it is on Expiry as "5 days left"; sell 10 — it shows 14 left; write off the rest — it is in Wastage.

### A411 · P2 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-05 (desktop 1.0.2) · Station routing needed the cloud — a till with no connection could not change where a category prints
Owner, 2026-10-05: "why does it have to save to the cloude cant it save local then push later if the till is fully
offline what happens since it cant reach the cloud?" A category tap (Printing › Stations) went to the cloud first and
changed nothing on the till until the cloud said yes. **BUILT (`apps/desktop/src/main/stationRouting.ts`):** the tap is
written to the till's own routing at once (tickets print that way straight away, online or not) and the station is
marked waiting (`maintenance_state` `station_routing_pending`); it is sent to the cloud now if possible, else before each
pull, in every push pass and on the 20 s beat. A pull (from the cloud or the branch server) lays the waiting set back
over what it wrote, so nothing undoes it while it waits. A cloud refusal (station deleted elsewhere, a category it does
not know) ends the wait and the screen says why; two tills editing one station — the later to reach the cloud wins
(whole set, never a diff). The till checks the person's role itself (stations.manage / products.manage, the cloud's
rule); the waiting set is sent later with the till's own sign-in (the person may have signed out), so A159's till
allowlist (`apps/server/src/lib/terminalWrites.ts`) now has exactly `PUT /api/stations/:id/categories` — creating,
renaming or deleting a station stays a PIN sign-in's (pinned in `tests/terminal-write-guard.test.mjs`). The screen shows "Saved on this till — … goes to the cloud and the other tills when the connection is back" and
"· waiting to sync". Creating, renaming and deleting stations still need the cloud. Test
`apps/desktop/test/station-routing-local.test.mjs` (19, real SQLite + syncEngine; 4 mutations bite). **Owner check:**
pull the network cable on a till, tick a category — it stays ticked with the amber note and a test order prints at that
station; plug back in — within ~20 s the note goes, and the web dashboard shows the same routing.

### A410 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-05 (desktop 1.0.2) · Every till talked to the cloud itself — the branch server was not the branch's link to the cloud
Owner, 2026-10-05: "if its a branch other tills rely on that server why would it save to cloud for other the server
should be the only till communicating with the cloud not other tills" — "if such a setting exist remove it". There was
no setting: every peer till was hard-wired to call the cloud directly (sales, menu pulls, sign-in renewals, manager
edits, voids/refunds, update checks and downloads) as well as the branch server (A160–A163 had built the server's half
of node-authority, but peers kept their own internet path). **BUILT:** a till with a branch server sends EVERY cloud
request to the server (`<node_url>/node/cloud/api/…` + the branch access code — `cloudGateway.ts`), and the server
forwards it to the cloud unchanged (the till's own token, device and idempotency headers) and streams the answer back
(`nodeGateway.ts`, route in `nodeServer.ts`). Only the cloud's `/api/` is reachable through it (not an open proxy); the
access code never leaves the branch. Server without internet → the till sees "no connection" (sales queue, retried) —
it never goes round the server; a wrong access code is "no connection" too, never a refused sign-in (which would
start A407's recovery). The branch server itself, office PCs and single tills are unchanged. Upgrade window only: a
server still on an older build (404, no gateway) — the till calls the cloud itself and logs it, until the server
updates. Every till call site goes through `cloudFetch` (sync engine, manager edits, enrolment, orders lookup,
voids/refunds, expense types, tech config/audit, update status + download). Test
`apps/desktop/test/branch-gateway.test.mjs` (22, the REAL node server on a real port + a stand-in cloud; 5 mutations
bite). **Owner check (two tills + server):** unplug a peer's internet but leave it on the shop network — it keeps
syncing sales and pulling menu changes through the server; unplug the server's internet — every till keeps selling
and their sales go up when it is back. **Approve 1.0.2 for every till of a branch together** (the server first is
best); a peer on 1.0.2 with a server still on 1.0.1 goes direct until the server updates.

### A408 · P2 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-05 (till, next build) · Station categories on the till "not selectable" — a refused save hid its own reason
Owner, 2026-10-05 (screenshot, Printers › Stations and routing, Drinks station, every category "prints nowhere"):

### A407 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-05 (cloud + till 1.0.0; migration 125) · A till's sign-in could be lost, with no way back but a new enrolment code
Owner, 2026-10-05: "how do we prevent this from ever happening" — "does it mean a till that is fully offline will one
day fail to log in?" — "if a till is rejected when it comes online after a long offline period i should get an email".
**Found while building:** the likely main cause of the Pollo sign-outs (A406) — a till's own session is "the owner, on
this device" (the enrolment code's creator), and `verify-pin` revoked "this user's sessions on this device" before
issuing a PIN session. The owner signing in on a till with their own PIN therefore revoked the till's session; ~15
minutes later its renewal was refused ("Please sign in again."). And the till never kept the A164 device secret, so it
could not recover, and a refused session made the PIN screen refuse everyone (no fallback to the till's own check).
**BUILT:**
- **migration 125:** `refresh_tokens.session_kind` (device = the till itself, pin = a person on a till, web = a browser),
  `user_devices.session_lost_at` / `session_lost_reason`.
- **cloud (`lib/tillSessions.ts`):** every session is stored with its kind; `verify-pin` never revokes when the PIN user is
  the till's own principal; password change/reset and "log out everywhere" go through `revokeBrowserSessions` (never a
  till: by kind, or a row naming an enrolled device). `/refresh` hands a till with no device secret a new one (only its
  own session, only to its own device) and clears a lost flag. `/device-token`: no secret or a refused one → the till is
  recorded as signed out (not for a till ZapTill blocked/retired); success or a new enrolment clears it.
  `scripts/check-till-sessions.mjs` (CI) fails the build on any revoke that could reach a till.
- **watchdog:** `tillsSignedOut` — CRITICAL (emailed at once, reminded every 3 h): "<client>: <till> is signed out and
  could not sign back in … Issue an enrolment code".
- **till (1.0.0):** keeps the device secret (enrolment, or handed over on a renewal; wrapped at rest; removed on sign-out);
  a refused renewal → `/api/auth/device-token` → signed back in, no person needed; a refused session at the PIN screen →
  the PIN is checked on the till (as offline) and the cashier sells — a wrong PIN stays a wrong PIN.
**Fully offline:** never affected — the PIN is checked on the till; after 30+ days offline the expired session is
replaced with the device secret when the internet returns; only a till with no secret (not yet renewed once on 1.0.0)
lands on the email. **Tests:** `apps/desktop/test/till-session-recovery.test.mjs` (9, real syncEngine and tokenStore, CI
step), `tests/till-sessions.test.mjs` (7), `tests/password-reset.test.mjs` (a marked till session survives). Mutations
(no device grant, secret not kept, a device session revocable, the PIN-path guard removed) each fail.

### A406 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-05 (cloud; no till release) · Tills fell back to the PIN screen with "Please sign in again."
Owner, 2026-10-05 (photo, Pollo Fried Chicken): "Why does it behave this way some tills are loosing their branch
configuration". **Causes (two, both cloud):**
1. **A402 (today) signed tills out.** A till signs in AS the owner — its refresh token carries the owner's user id
   (enrol / device-token). "Signed out everywhere" on an owner's password change or reset revoked those too, so every
   till of the business lost its session at its next renewal, and the till cannot recover alone (it never kept the
   A164 device secret) — someone had to sign in again.
2. **A391 (2026-10-04) changed what an expired token says.** An expired ZapTill access token (15 minutes, renewed all
   day) fell through to the Supabase branch, which since A391 answers 401 "Please sign in again." — the words the till
   then shows when a renewal fails, instead of its own "This till was signed out" message.
**BUILT:** `lib/passwordReset.ts` revokes the owner's browser sessions only — a session whose device_hint is one of
the business's enrolled devices (user_devices) is kept. `middleware/auth.ts`: a ZapTill token that is only expired gets
401 "Invalid or expired token" (TOKEN_EXPIRED); a non-ZapTill token still meets the A391 rule. **Tests:**
`tests/password-reset.test.mjs` (12: a till's session survives a reset; an expired token is TOKEN_EXPIRED, a foreign
one SIGN_IN_AGAIN). **Recovery for a till already signed out:** the owner signs in on it once (Sign out / switch
account → enrol). **Next (till, 1.0.1):** keep the device secret at enrolment and use `/api/auth/device-token` when a
renewal is refused, so a till never needs a person to sign it back in.

### A397 · P2 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-04 (v0.6.38) · Printing to a Windows printer fails on a slow PC, the ticket is dropped and the message is a command line
Field, 2026-10: on one PC every `printer:` station (Kitchen, Dispatch, Till) failed Test print with "Command failed:
powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command". **Cause:** a `printer:` target prints through PowerShell, which
built the winspool helper (C#, `Add-Type` → csc.exe) afresh for EVERY ticket, inside an 8-second limit. On a slow PC
(first print after start-up, antivirus scanning PowerShell) that is more than 8 s; Node killed PowerShell, and with no
error text the classifier fell back to the command line and called it "a fault in ZapTill" with `retryable: false` —
so the background queue gave up on the kitchen ticket. **BUILT (0.6.38, `shared/printing/src/transport.ts`):**
- a `printer:` target gets 20 s (`SPOOLER_TIMEOUT_MS`); network, share and device targets keep 8 s;
- the helper is built ONCE to `%TEMP%\zaptill-raw-<hash of the C#>.dll` and loaded from there afterwards (fast); if the
  file cannot be built, moved or loaded (antivirus, rights, a broken file) the script builds it in memory exactly as
  before — the cache can make printing faster, never stop it. A changed C# gets a new file (the hash);
- a timeout is its own outcome (`spoolerOutcome`, pure): `timedOut`, retryable (the spool tries again — the next try
  uses the helper this one built), not "ours" and not "the printer"; the till's Test print says "Windows took too long
  to accept the job. Press Test print again … open the printer's queue in Windows …";
- the script prints `ZAPTILL-SENT` once the spooler has the bytes: a run killed after that counts as printed, so a
  retry never prints the ticket twice;
- Node's "Command failed: powershell.exe …" is never shown; "the Windows print helper stopped without giving a reason".
**Tests:** `shared/printing/test/spooler.test.ts` §4 (real `spoolerOutcome`, the script's order: cached → build to
file → in-memory fallback → send → mark), `tests/print-timeout.test.mjs` (Test print and the message). Mutations
(retryable false, no SENT mark, raw command line, no in-memory fallback, 8 s) each fail a test. **Not testable here:**
the PowerShell itself runs only on Windows — confirm on the PC that failed: Test print on each `printer:` station, the
first may take a few seconds, the next ones should be quick; `%TEMP%` then holds one `zaptill-raw-….dll`.

### A395 · P2 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-04 (cloud + dashboard; migration 121) · Nothing recorded what is owed to suppliers, what was paid, or goods sent back
Owner, 2026-10-04: after the stock take — supplier bills and payables, with returns to supplier ("Yes proceed"). Before:
suppliers, purchase orders and goods received notes existed, but no bill, no payment, no balance, no return. **BUILT:**
Stock › Suppliers shows what is owed (total, overdue, due in 7 days) and each supplier's balance; **Account** opens a
supplier: bills (the supplier's invoice no., date, pay-within terms → due date; open / part paid / overdue / paid),
payments (M-Pesa, bank, cash, cheque, other, with a reference; against a bill — never more than it still owes — or on
account), returns, a statement with a running balance (printable), ageing (not yet due / 1–30 / 31–60 / 61–90 / 90+), and
**deliveries not billed yet** (GRNs from the supplier's purchase orders, valued at cost — "Bill it"; one open bill per
delivery). A bill or payment is voided with a reason, never deleted; a bill with payments cannot be voided. **Return
goods**: products and/or ingredients leave the branch at once (atomic, never more than the branch holds, a movement
naming the return) and the supplier owes the credit at cost. Balance = open bills − payments − return credits
(lib/payables.ts). New permission `payables.manage` — the owner's by default (MANAGER_DENY; migration 121 grants it to
nobody); returns need `inventory.receive`. A payment recorded here is not an expense and does not touch a drawer (the
screen says so). Tests: `tests/supplier-payables.test.mjs` (12; 6 mutations bite), `scripts/test-migration-121.mjs` (7).
Closes when the owner has billed, paid and returned against a real supplier.

### A394 · P2 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-04 (cloud + dashboard + web POS + till; migration 120) · No stock take — a count was a printed sheet showing the system figure and one-item corrections
Owner, 2026-10-04: "We are missing a stock take module" — "Yes the count should be blind, I would recommend freeze but we
leave that as a feature which the owner will decide". Before: Inventory printed a count sheet WITH the system quantity,
and a count went back in one item at a time as a Correction — no record of the count, no differences, no review.
**BUILT:** (1) **Stock counts** (owner: Stock › Stock Counts; manager: Inventory › Stock count) — start a count at a
branch: stocked products, ingredients or both; everything the branch stocks, or chosen categories (fuel excluded: the
dip). One open count per branch. (2) **Blind** — the person counting types what is on the shelf and never sees the
system's figure: the cloud records what the system held at the moment each item was counted (`expected_qty`) and sends it
only to someone holding `inventory.adjust` (the owner by default); while a branch counts, the counted items' figures are
hidden on the manager's stock screens too; the printed sheet has no system column. (3) **Hand in → review → post** — the
reviewer sees each difference and its value at cost (short / over / net), sends chosen items back to be counted again
(blank, blind; the first count kept), and posts: stock changes by the DIFFERENCE through the atomic RPCs (never "set
to"), so sales and deliveries after the count stay; each change is a movement naming the count. A post is claimed once
and can be finished if interrupted. (4) **Selling while counting** — each item is compared with what the system held
when it was counted; a till's sale made before an item was counted that reaches the cloud afterwards is found and taken
off what was expected (ingredient sale movements now carry their order, migration 120). (5) **Freeze — the owner's
switch** (Stock Counts page, recommended): an item in a count cannot be sold — on the web POS (at the counter and at
payment, STOCK_COUNT_FROZEN) and on the tills (pos/init `stockCount`, within ~20 s; local schema 67) — until it has been
counted, then it is released at once. A till's sale already made is never refused. New permission `inventory.count`
(manager tier, migration 120). Tests: `tests/stock-take.test.mjs` (22; 7 mutations bite), `scripts/test-migration-120.mjs`
(7). The till part ships with the next desktop build. Closes when the owner has run a real count end to end.

### A389 · P2 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-04 (cloud + web; the till's import rides the next till build) · Uploading the same menu again added copies — of products' choices above all
Owner, 2026-10-04: "if i upload the same product it reuploads the same product it does not check if the product exist"
— then "the variants were added on the same product which were there". **Cause:** the products import did match by name
(proved: the real route run twice with one file — 0 added, 2 updated), but only on `trim().toLowerCase()`, so a name with a
non-breaking / zero-width / double space (Excel, WhatsApp and web copies carry them) was a "new" product; an archived copy
could be the one matched; only the first 1,000 products were read. The **choices** import (Upgrades & Spices → POST
/api/variants/bulk) looked a group up by its EXACT name with `maybeSingle()`: "Drink size" ≠ "Drink Size", and once a
product held two groups of one name `maybeSingle` errored, was read as "none", and **every** upload added another. The
till's import removed only the first same-named group, so an existing copy survived. **BUILT:** one comparison for every
import, `importKey` (lib/productImport.ts: NFKC, hidden spaces dropped, spaces collapsed, case) — products, categories,
choice groups, recipes, ingredients; products read in pages, an ACTIVE product preferred over an archived one; choices:
this product's own groups (never a shared or combo-component group) matched on the key, the oldest kept and **copies an
earlier upload left removed** (options with them) — a re-upload heals; DELETE removes every copy. The upload result says
**"N added · M updated"** and names the new products (dashboard Menu upload and CSV import), so a surprise is seen at once;
"K duplicate groups removed" when it heals. Till › Menu › Import: every same-named choice / add-on group is replaced.
Tests: `tests/menu-reimport.test.mjs` (12, the compiled routes over HTTP). Products duplicated BEFORE this stay until
deleted by hand (Products page); their choices heal on the next upload. Closes when the owner re-uploads the menu and sees
"0 added".

Owner, 2026-10-03: "let us do the ZapTill rename" (the domain moved in A385). **BUILT (0.6.36):** every "SwiftPOS" a

### A382 · P1 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-03 (v0.6.34) · A bar trading past midnight was locked mid-service — the business day ended at 00:00
Found 2026-10-03 thinking as a hotel owner (lead review, owner agreed): the till's business date was the calendar date
(`dayService.ts` `businessDateNow`), and an unclosed earlier day refuses every sale (`checkDayGate`) — so at 00:00 a hotel
bar mid-service read "Trading day … was never closed. A manager must count the cash and close it", and with 24-hour
operation the 2-hour grace still locked it at 02:00. **BUILT (0.6.34):** the owner's **"Business day ends at"**
(`business_day_cutoff`, 00:00–06:00 in half hours, default 00:00 = as before; Settings › Business; per branch in the
branch overrides) — `shared/businessDay.ts` (copied to cloud, till, web). Till (local schema 64, REQUIRED 64): the business
date, the day gate, the 24-hour grace (from the cut-off, not midnight) and History's "Today" follow it; pulled with
pos/init and relayed by a branch server. Cloud: the setting validated (business and branch), pos/init sends it, every
report in `routes/reports.ts` and the daily email count the business day (`lib/dayCutoff.ts`, cached a minute); the
fuel "today" report fixed from the UTC date to the East Africa business date. Web POS: History's "today" follows it (the
web POS has no day lock). **Not changed:** the dashboard's date pickers still default to the calendar date (a report
opened between midnight and the cut-off shows the new day — pick yesterday); `reports-daily`, `reports-export` and the
expenses list keep their own date parsing. **Tests:** `tests/business-day.test.mjs` (8),
`apps/desktop/test/business-day.test.mjs` (14, real main on SQLite with a set clock; CI step). Closes when a till with a
04:00 cut-off sells at 01:30 and locks after 04:00 on target.

### A381 · P3 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-12 (till 1.0.8, with A450) · The branch server does not pass a logo change to the other tills
Found 2026-10-03 answering the owner ("Assume i change the logo in the server in an ofline setup will it be replicated
across?"). A logo uploaded on any till (Tech → branding) is saved on that till at once (its screen and receipts use it)
and marked pending; at the next sync with internet it is sent to the cloud (`syncEngine.ts` `queueBrandingPush`,
`PUT /api/business/branding`), and every other till gets it at ITS next catalogue pull from the cloud. Nothing goes over
the shop network: the server's reference bundle to its tills carries no branding (`referenceBundle.ts` — "a node bundle,
which relays no branding today"). So in a shop without internet, only the machine it was uploaded on shows the new logo;
the others change when the internet returns. **Fix (when wanted):** add the branding row (and the receipt logo switch) to
the server's reference bundle, applied on the till like the cloud's, unless the till has its own upload pending.
**BUILT 2026-10-12 (owner: "add 1 and 2"):** the branch server's bundle carries its branding (`referenceBundle.ts`
`nodeIdentity`), applied on a till like the cloud's (not while its own upload is pending); a logo set on a till behind a
server is handed to it at once (`POST /node/branding`, which moves the server's change counter so a till with no internet
pulls now). Test `apps/desktop/test/business-identity.test.mjs`.

### A380 · P3 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-13 (till 1.0.11) · The server's nightly backups sit on the same disk as its database
**BUILT 2026-10-13 (owner: "A380 is okay we can build it"):** Tech page › Backups — **Choose backup folder…** (a folder picker; a backup is written there at once to prove it — if it cannot be written the old folder stays and the reason is shown), **Use the default**, and an amber warning while the backups sit on the database's own disk (`maintenance.ts` `onDatabaseDisk`: by volume; a network share is another machine). Only a technician signed in may change it (logged). Also: a failed backup no longer counts as the last backup and is tried again after an hour (it waited 20 hours). Test `apps/desktop/test/backup-folder.test.mjs` (13); mutations confirmed.
Owner, 2026-10-03: "the server holds the hotel data for ever right?" — then "yes we add the backup folder setting later
not now add that in the audit tracker". The branch server keeps every branch record (it never prunes — `maintenance.ts`
`pruneReplicas` skips the node) and takes a nightly SQLite backup, keeping 14 (`DEFAULT_SNAPSHOT_KEEP`). The backups go to
`<userData>/backups` on the same PC unless `maintenance_state.backup_dir` is set, and nothing on screen sets it — the Tech
page only shows the folder. A failed disk or a stolen PC takes the database and its backups together; what had not reached
the cloud yet is lost. **Fix (when wanted):** a Tech-page setting to choose the backup folder (a USB drive or second disk),
tested by writing a backup there at once and showing its time; a warning on the Tech page while the folder is on the
database's own disk.

### A379 · P2 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-02 (v0.6.33) · Free delivery — the shop pays the rider, the customer pays no fee
Owner, 2026-10-02: "in adition to the delivery with delivery fee can we add an option of free delivery where its not a must
for the cashier to key in delivery fee? but that can be turned on and of by the hotel owner" — then, correcting the first
build: "though this free delivery the rider is still paid by the shop so delivery fee is a must but the customer does not
pay it". **BUILT (0.6.33):** the owner's rule `delivery_free_allowed` (`shared/reversalRules.ts`, off by default,
owner-only like the void/refund rules, carried by pos/init's `reversalRules` and relayed by a branch node) offers the
cashier a **Free delivery** tick on a delivery (till and web POS). The fee is still REQUIRED (`deliveryProblem`
unchanged) and is still paid to the rider in cash from the drawer (the existing pay-out paths, fee > 0); ticked, the order
is `delivery_free` and the customer pays the bill alone (`customerDeliveryFee`). **Migration 115**: `orders.delivery_free`
and `create_order_atomic` reconciling the legs to total + tip (+ the fee only when not free); `/pay` the same. Till: local
schema 63 (`orders` + `held_orders.delivery_free`; REQUIRED 63), the payload, a held tab, the branch relay, the copied web
sales. Receipt (`shared/printing`): "Delivery: FREE", the fee not in PAY. Z-report: "Delivery fees (in payments)" counts only
the customers' fees; a new "Free deliveries (shop paid)" line; "Paid to riders" includes both. History shows what the
customer paid. Switched on the web (Settings › Business › **Voids, refunds & delivery**) and the till (Manager → Settings,
as the owner). **Also in 0.6.33 (owner, 2026-10-02: "I need all 3 before taging"):** *free delivery above an amount* — the
owner's `delivery_free_over` (Settings / Manager → Settings; empty = off): a delivery whose bill reaches it is free
automatically (`autoFreeDelivery`; the tick shown ticked and locked), same money as a ticked one; *the riders summary* — the
till's Z-report (screen and paper) lists each rider: deliveries, what they were paid, the free ones the shop paid
(`riderSummary`; voided sales left out; none on a blind close). **Tests:** `tests/free-delivery.test.mjs` (17),
`apps/desktop/test/free-delivery.test.mjs` (13, real main on SQLite), `scripts/test-migration-115.mjs` (7, Postgres),
`shared/printing` delivery test (+3); older pins moved
(`reversal-rules`, `prospect-features`, `cross-sync`, `owner-0629`, `web-receipt-money`, desktop `order-notes`). Closes when a
free delivery is rung on T1: the customer pays the bill, the drawer pays the rider, the Z-report shows it apart.

accent only); `/login` refuses an unknown address BEFORE checking the password and opens only the address's business
(`NOT_THIS_BUSINESS`, `ownedTenantBusiness`); `/pos-login` matches only that business's people (same answer as a wrong
email); CORS admits `https://<one label>.<TENANT_ROOT_DOMAIN>`; admin `PATCH /clients/:id { subdomain }` validated, a taken
address 409; the client page shows the full address. Web: dashboard sign-in and web POS sign-in show the client's logo and
name, send the subdomain, and show "This address is not set up" for an unknown one. Admin portal: Overview › Sign-in
address (set / change / clear). **Off until configured:** `TENANT_ROOT_DOMAIN` (Render) and `VITE_TENANT_ROOT_DOMAIN`
(Vercel, dashboard) — the same root, e.g. `swiftpos.co.ke`; a wildcard DNS record `*.<root>` → Vercel and the wildcard
domain on the dashboard's Vercel project. Unset, every address behaves as before. **Not covered:** the till (signs in by
enrolment, not an address); a client's logo in emails. **Test:** `tests/tenant-signin.test.mjs` (16),
`scripts/test-migration-114.mjs` (6); a browser run of the built dashboard on `africanfries.<root>` (logo + name, the
subdomain sent, "Not this business", an unknown address, the main address unchanged). Closes when a client signs in on
their own address in production.

### A377 · P2 · FIX BUILT 2026-10-02 (v0.6.32) · A 32-bit Windows till could not run SwiftPOS (64-bit installer only)
Owner, 2026-10-02: a client's till is **Windows 10 32-bit, 4 GB** — "use combined installer". The desktop was built for
64-bit Windows only (`electron-builder --win nsis`, `SwiftPOS-<v>-x64.exe`). No code change was needed: Electron 43
publishes win32-ia32, better-sqlite3 (the only native module) is rebuilt per arch at packaging, the till prints without
the Go bridge. **BUILT (desktop 0.6.32, build only):** `electron-builder.config.js` — NSIS target `arch: ['x64','ia32']`
(ONE installer that installs the right build), fixed name `${productName}-${version}.${ext}` → `SwiftPOS-0.6.32.exe`;
`release.yml` builds `--x64 --ia32` and its check looks for `SwiftPOS-<v>.exe`; `pack:installer` the same. The cloud's
update feed already serves any `.exe` of the approved release; a 32-bit till updates to the 32-bit build. About twice the
download of a 64-bit-only installer. **Not covered:** Windows 7/8 (this Electron does not run there); the web-POS Go print
bridge stays 64-bit (`GOARCH=386` on request). **Test:** `tests/desktop-installer-32bit.test.mjs` (6). Closes when the
32-bit till installs and sells.
**Released 2026-10-02 (run 48, green):** `SwiftPOS-0.6.32.exe` 204 MB, x64 + ia32, `latest.yml` checked from the public
link. Runs 45–47 failed: the tag `v0.6.32` was pushed on main's A376 merge `11b8300` (0.6.31) — a stale local tag pushed
again — so each built a 0.6.31 installer, overwrote the v0.6.31 release's files (same 0.6.31 till code) and failed only at
the last check. Re-tagged by commit (`c1619c6`); the deleted tag had turned the release into a DRAFT, which the last check
passed and the owner published by hand. **Release run hardened:** a first step stops in seconds when the tag's
`apps/desktop/package.json` version is not the tag's (and prints how to tag); the release step re-publishes a draft
(still pre-release); the last check refuses a draft. Tag from dev with `git push origin origin/dev:refs/tags/vX.Y.Z`.

### A376 · P1 · CLOSED 2026-10-02 (verified on target) · A new client's till could not be enrolled — "Could not resolve the business owner for this code"
**Verified on target 2026-10-02:** deployed (merged to main); the new client's till enrolled from the admin portal. **CLOSED.**
Owner, 2026-10-02: a client registered that day got no enrolment code in the admin portal ("Enrol till"); an older test
client did. The banner at the top of the client page read **"Could not resolve the business owner for this code."** (the
admin was looking at the branch list, so it looked like nothing happened). Cause: a till's enrolment code is issued under
the client OWNER's staff record (the redeemed till runs as the owner — sales point at a staff record, an admin is not one),
and `resolveOwnerUserId` found that record ONLY by matching `businesses.email` to a staff email. That is the business
CONTACT email: self-signup stores the form's contact email when one is given, and the owner can change it in Settings ›
Business › Profile — then nothing matches and every code is refused. **Fix:** `lib/ownerBusiness.ts` — the owner's SIGN-IN
email first (`businesses.owner_id` → the auth user), then `businesses.email` (unchanged for every client that worked), then
the business's one active `owner`-role user; an email shared by two people is never guessed between (pure
`pickOwnerUserId`). Still refuses when nobody resolves. Admin portal: an enrolment error now shows beside the branches, not
only at the top. **Workaround until deployed:** set the client's Profile contact email to the owner's sign-in email.
**Test:** `tests/owner-resolve.test.mjs` (8; 3 mutations bite). Closes when the new client's till enrols.
